children.translated_text: The <s>Padyāvalī</s>, composed by connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s>,
whose words are beautiful through connection with <s>Mukunda</s>, an ocean of waves of delight —
lovely, dispelling all darkness, gradually
is compiled for the delight of the collection of poetic works. ||1||

body.translated_text: At the commencement of the work, the auspicious invocation:

children.translated_text: Salutation to the lotus-eyed one,
who delights in the playing of the flute,
who drinks the nectar of <s>Rādhā</s>'s lips,
adorned with a garland of forest [flowers]. ||2||
Tenderly gazing upon devotees who bow [before him], rivaling the blue lotus,
taken as the support of meditation by those absorbed in <s>samādhi</s>, for the attainment of well-being,
bestowing aesthetic relish upon the eyes of <s>Rādhā</s>, as the sole great treasury of beauty —

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ kurutāṃ bhavārti-śamanaṃ netre tanur vā hareḥ ||3||
children.translated_text: may the eyes — or the body — of <s>Hari</s> bring about the cessation of the sorrow of existence for you. ||3||
Those [arms] whose peacock-feather ornaments were stained with the muddy essence at the foot of <s>Govardhana</s>,
those which were the playful cushions of the young women of <s>Vraja</s> in the recesses of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
and those which are fragrant with [massage] oil from the gift-water of <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> [the elephant] —

children.text: te vo maṅgalam ādiśantu satataṃ kaṃsa-dviṣo bāhavaḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: may those arms of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> always bestow auspiciousness upon you. ||4||
At evening, [bearing] the names that serve as signals for calling back all the herds of cows,
[being] the perfected <s>mantra</s>-syllables accomplished in the art of forcibly stealing the hearts of groups of cowherd women,

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ vaḥ samantād dadhatu madhu-bhidaḥ keli-gopāla-mūrteḥ
children.translated_text: may the sounds of the flute bestow prosperity upon you from all sides — those of <s>Madhubhid</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) in his playful cowherd form,
drawing forth with delight rows of enraptured deer in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. ||5||

children.text: ambhobhiḥ sthalatāṃ sthalaṃ jaladhitāṃ dhūlīlavaḥ śailatāṃ
children.translated_text: Water becomes land, land becomes the ocean, a speck of dust becomes a mountain,

children.text: śailī mṛt-kaṇatāṃ tṛṇaṃ kuliśatāṃ vajraṃ tṛṇa-kṣīṇatām |
children.translated_text: a mountain becomes a grain of earth, a blade of grass becomes a thunderbolt, a diamond becomes as feeble as a straw,

children.text: vahniḥ śītalatāṃ himaṃ vahanatām āyāti yasyecchayā
children.translated_text: fire becomes cold, frost becomes blazing — by whose will [all this occurs].
Salutation to that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is passionately addicted to the marvelous caprice of [his divine] sport! ||6||
Because of [his] parental affection, because of [his] granting of fearlessness, because of [his] quenching the suffering of the distressed,
because of [his] generosity, because of [his] destroying sin, because of [his] leading to the incomparable state of blessedness —

children.text: sevyaḥ śrī-patir eva sarva-jagatām ete yataḥ sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) alone is to be served by all the worlds, for these are the witnesses:

children.text: prahlādaś ca vibhīṣaṇaś ca karirāṭ pāñcalya-halyā dhruvaḥ ||7||
children.translated_text: <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the king of elephants [<s>Gajendra</s>], <s>Draupadī</s>, <s>Ahalyā</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s>. ||7||

children.text: vyādhasyācaraṇaṃ dhruvasya ca vayo vidyā gajendrasya kā
children.translated_text: What was the conduct of the hunter [<s>Vyādha</s>]? And what was the age of <s>Dhruva</s>? What learning had the king of elephants [<s>Gajendra</s>]?

children.text: kubjāyāḥ kim u nāma rūpam adhikaṃ kiṃ tat sudāmno dhanam |
children.translated_text: What indeed was the beauty of the hunchback [<s>Kubjā</s>]? What wealth had <s>Sudāmā</s>?

children.text: vaṃśaḥ ko vidurasya yādavapater ugrasya kiṃ pauruṣaṃ
children.translated_text: What was the lineage of <s>Vidura</s>? What was the valor of <s>Ugrasena</s>, the lord of the <s>Yādavas</s>?

children.text: bhaktyā tuṣyati kevalaṃ na ca guṇair bhakti-priyo mādhavaḥ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s>, the lover of devotion (<s>bhakti-priya</s>), is pleased by devotion alone, not by [worldly] qualities. ||8||

children.text: anucitam ucitaṃ vā karma ko'yaṃ vibhāgo
children.translated_text: Whether the action is improper or proper — what is this distinction?
O Lord, let the <s>yoga</s> of devotion (<s>bhaktiyoga</s>) be most firmly [established].
The king of poison [<s>Śiva</s>] showers abundant nectar; the moon [does the same] —

children.text: dvayam api sa maheśo nirviśeṣaṃ bibharti ||9||
children.translated_text: both, that great lord (<s>Maheśa</s>) bears without distinction. ||9||
If, O crusher of <s>Madhu</s>, a discerning one
performs or abandons the service of your feet in the heart,
then all sin in the three worlds

children.text: kṛtam akṛtaṃ na kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ ca sarvam ||10||
children.translated_text: that was done becomes undone, and what was not done becomes done. ||10||

children.text: kāṣāyān na ca bhojanādi-niyamān no vā vane vāsato
children.translated_text: Not from the saffron robe, not from restrictions on food and the like, not from dwelling in the forest,

children.text: vyākhyānād atha vā muni-vrata-bharāc cittodbhavaḥ kṣīyate |
children.translated_text: not from lecturing, nor from bearing the ascetic's vow — is the mind-born [desire] destroyed.
But from even the slightest beginning of the worship of the lotus-feet
of <s>Govinda</s>, who sports on the banks of the overflowing daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> mountain [<s>Yamunā</s>]. ||11||

children.text: alam alam iyam eva prāṇināṃ pātakānāṃ
children.translated_text: Enough, enough! This alone is sufficient for the removal of the sins
of living beings — the utterance '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!'
If devotion, dense with bliss, arises toward <s>Mukunda</s>,
then the sovereignty-<s>Lakṣmī</s> of liberation rolls at [his] lotus-feet. ||12||
May the heart of the devotee, melting with happiness through love alone,
not [merely] be the worship conducted with various offerings to the Friend of the Afflicted.

children.text: yāvat kṣud asti jaṭhare jaraṭhā pipāsā
children.translated_text: So long as there is hunger in the belly and stubborn thirst,
so long are food and drink indeed for your happiness! ||13||
let it be cultivated, if it can be obtained from anywhere!
For that, ardent longing (<s>laulya</s>) alone is the price;
it cannot be obtained by the merits of tens of millions of births. ||14||

body.translated_text: A mind imbued with the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic relish) of devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.translated_text: Knowledge has been weighed on the scale;
<s>prema</s> (divine love) has not been weighed on the scale.
<s>Siddhi</s> (perfection) indeed has been weighed on the scale;
the name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has not been weighed on the scale. ||15||

body.translated_text: Now, the greatness of the Holy Name (<s>nāmamāhātmya</s>):

children.translated_text: Destroying all sin at once
upon its arising, for the entire world —
like the sun [dispelling] the ocean of darkness —
victorious is the Name of <s>Hari</s>, the auspiciousness of the world! ||16||

children.text: caturṇāṃ vedānāṃ hṛdayam idam ākṛṣya hariṇā
children.translated_text: Having extracted the essence of the four <s>Vedas</s>, by <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: caturbhir yad varṇaiḥ sphuṭam aghaṭi nārāyaṇa-padam |
children.translated_text: with four syllables the word <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> was manifestly fashioned.

children.text: tad etad gāyanto vayam aniśam ātmānam adhunā
children.translated_text: Singing that [Name] ceaselessly, we now

children.text: punīmo jānīmo na hari-paritoṣāya kim api ||17||
children.translated_text: purify ourselves; we do not know anything [else] for the satisfaction of <s>Hari</s>. ||17||
Let these <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having attained the sovereignty

children.text: svārājyaṃ pratipadya nirbhayam amī muktā bhavantu dvijāḥ |
children.translated_text: cultivated through <s>yoga</s>, <s>śruti</s>, logic, and meditation on the path of solitary forests, be fearlessly liberated!
But for us, who relish the Name of that dark-complexioned abode,
[shining] like rows of blue lotuses blooming in the hollows of <s>kadamba</s>-groves — may birth [continue] even for a hundred thousand [lives]! ||18||
The treasury of all that is auspicious, the churner of the impurity of <s>Kali</s>, the purifier of the pure,

children.text: pātheyaṃ yan mumukṣoḥ sapadi parapadaprāptaye procyamānam |
children.translated_text: the provision for the seeker of liberation, proclaimed for the immediate attainment of the supreme abode,
the sole resting place of the words of the greatest poets, the life of good people,

children.text: bījaṃ dharma-drumasya prabhavatu bhavatāṃ bhūtaye kṛṣṇa-nāma ||19||
children.translated_text: the seed of the tree of <s>dharma</s> — may the Name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> bring about your welfare! ||19||
Sins tremble; the grandeur of delusion falls into a swoon;
the illustrious <s>Citragupta</s>, the [karmic] accountant, anxiously tears up the record of the night [of sins].
Joyfully, <s>Brahmā</s> makes preparation for the offering of the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) welcome-rite —

children.text: vaktuṃ nāmni taveśvarābhilaṣite brūmaḥ kim anyat param ||20||
children.translated_text: when your Name, O Lord, is desired to be spoken. What more need we say? ||20||
Who would be the lord of the City of the Dead [<s>Yama</s>]?
And who would be his servant?
[If] the Name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sole auspiciousness of the world,
takes its seat upon the throne of the throat! ||21||
Cleansing the mirror of the mind, extinguishing the great forest-fire of material existence,
spreading the moonlight of the white lotus of supreme good fortune, the life of the bride of knowledge,
increasing the ocean of bliss, at every step the tasting of full nectar,
bathing the entire self — all-glorious is the congregational chanting (<s>saṅkīrtana</s>) of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! ||22||
Of the <s>brahmāṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs), numbering more than <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions),

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ yac cetanā vā yad aṃśaḥ |
children.translated_text: whatever sovereignty or consciousness exists — that is [but] a portion [of the Name].
That effulgence, manifested, is the Name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.text: tan me sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ jīvanaṃ ca ||23||
children.translated_text: that is my goal, my means, and my very life. ||23||

children.text: viṣṇor nāmaiva puṃsāḥ śamalam apaharat puṇyam utpādayac ca
children.translated_text: The Name of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone removes the sin of a person, produces merit,
[produces] detachment from the enjoyment of positions such as <s>Brahmā</s>'s, and devotion to the two blessed feet of the <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: Tattva-jñānaṃ ca viṣṇor iha mṛti-janana-bhrānti-bījaṃ ca dagdhvā
children.translated_text: It [bestows] knowledge of reality about <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and having burned the seed of the delusion of birth and death,

children.text: saṃpūrṇānanda-bodhe mahati ca puruṣaṃ sthāpayitvā nivṛttam ||24||
children.translated_text: it establishes the person in the great state of complete bliss-consciousness, and then ceases. ||24||
The Name is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>),
an embodiment of consciousness and <s>rasa</s>.
Complete, pure, eternally liberated —
because of the non-difference of the Name and the Named. ||25||
Sweeter than the sweetest, this auspiciousness of auspiciousnesses,
the true fruit of the creeper of all the <s>Vedas</s>, of the nature of pure consciousness —
even if sung once, whether with faith or with neglect,
O best of <s>Bhṛgus</s>, the Name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> delivers a mere human being. ||26||

children.text: svargārthīyā vyavasitir asau dīnayaty eva lokān
children.translated_text: The resolution aimed at heaven only impoverishes people;
the expectation of liberation merely makes a person a sharer in affliction.
The practice of <s>yoga</s> is supremely tasteless — what is the use of such efforts?

children.text: sarvaṃ tyaktvā mama tu rasanā kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti rautu ||27||
children.translated_text: Abandoning everything, let my tongue simply cry out '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' ||27||

children.text: sadā sarvatrāste nanu vimalam ādyaṃ tava padaṃ
children.translated_text: Indeed, your primordial, spotless abode (<s>pada</s>) exists always and everywhere;

children.text: tathāpy ekaṃ stokaṃ na hi bhava-taroḥ patram abhinat |
children.translated_text: yet it has not broken even one small leaf of the tree of worldly existence.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ jihvāgra-sthaṃ tava tu bhagavan-nāma nikhilaṃ
children.translated_text: But your divine Name, O Lord, when placed on the tip of the tongue for a moment,

children.text: sa-mūlaṃ sambhāraṃ kaṣati katarat sevyam anayoḥ ||28||
children.translated_text: pulls up the entire apparatus with its roots. Which of these two is to be resorted to? ||28||
The attractress of the minds of the wise, the eradicatress of sins to the highest degree,
accessible even to the <s>caṇḍāla</s> and the mute people of the world, and the controller of the sovereignty of liberation —

children.text: no dīkṣāṃ na ca sat-kriyāṃ na ca puraścaryāṃ manāg īkṣate
children.translated_text: it regards not initiation, nor proper rites, nor preliminary practices (<s>puraścaryā</s>) even slightly.
This <s>mantra</s>, consisting of the Name of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, bears fruit by merely touching the tongue. ||29||
To be selected, to be examined,
to be contemplated again and again —
like the riches of a miser,
may your Names be [thus cherished] by us! ||30||
In [your] Names, you have manifested your entire <s>śakti</s> (power) in many ways;
therein, no time is prescribed for remembrance.
Such, O Lord, is your grace. But even so,
such is my misfortune that no attachment [to your Name] has arisen [in me]. ||31||

body.translated_text: Now, the chanting of the Name (<s>nāmakīrtana</s>):

body.text:
tṛṇād api sunīcena
taror iva sahiṣṇunā |
amāninā mānadena
kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ ||32|| tasyaiva || (CC 3.20.21)
body.translated_text: One should always chant the name of <s>Hari</s>, being humbler than a blade of grass, more forbearing than a tree, offering respect to others while expecting none for oneself. ||32|| By the same: (CC 3.20.21)

children.translated_text: '<s>Śrī Rāma</s>!' '<s>Janārdana</s>!' 'Lord of the Worlds!' '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!'
'Bliss!' 'Compassionate One!' 'Beloved of <s>Kamalā</s>!' '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!'
Plunged in the waves and billows of the great nectar-ocean of the blessed divine Names,

children.text: rmuhyantaṃ galad-aśru-netramavaśaṃ māṃ nātha nityaṃ kuru ||33||
children.translated_text: drowning again and again, with tears streaming from the eyes, helpless — O Lord, make me always thus! ||33||
O beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O compassionate one, O lotus-naveled one,
O beloved of liberation, O <s>Mukunda</s>, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>!
The garland of [your] Names — like a string of spotless pearls,
surpassing the beauty of <s>Lakṣmī</s> — let me place it upon my throat! ||34||

children.text: kṛṣṇa rāma mukunda vāmana vāsudeva jagadguro
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Rāma</s>! <s>Mukunda</s>! <s>Vāmana</s>! <s>Vāsudeva</s>! O teacher of the world!

children.text: matsya kacchapa nārasiṃha varāha rāghava pāhi mām |
children.translated_text: <s>Matsya</s>! <s>Kacchapa</s>! <s>Nārasiṃha</s>! <s>Varāha</s>! <s>Rāghava</s>! Protect me!
O one praised by <s>devas</s>, <s>dānavas</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and the foremost among sages, O treasury of compassion!
O son of <s>Devakī</s>, grant me unwavering devotion to your feet! ||35||

children.text: he gopālaka he kṛpā-jala-nidhe he sindhu-kanyā-pate
children.translated_text: O Cowherd (<s>Gopālaka</s>)! O ocean of the waters of compassion! O consort of the Daughter of the Ocean (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)!

children.text: he kaṃsāntaka he gajendra-karuṇā-pārīṇa he mādhava |
children.translated_text: O slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>! O one experienced in compassion for <s>Gajendra</s>! O <s>Mādhava</s>!

children.text: he rāmānuja he jagat-traya-guro he puṇḍarīkākṣa māṃ
children.translated_text: O younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>! O teacher of the three worlds! O lotus-eyed one!

children.text: he gopījana-nātha pālaya paraṃ jānāmi na tvāṃ vinā ||36||
children.translated_text: O Lord of the <s>Gopī</s> women! Protect me! I know no one supreme but you. ||36||
<s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>! Lotus-eyed one! <s>Śrī Rāma</s>! Consort of <s>Sītā</s>!
<s>Govinda</s>! <s>Acyuta</s>! Joy of <s>Nanda</s>! <s>Mukunda</s>! Bliss! <s>Dāmodara</s>!
<s>Viṣṇu</s>! <s>Rāghava</s>! <s>Vāsudeva</s>! Man-lion (<s>Nṛhari</s>)! Crest-jewel of the Lord of Gods!
O helmsman of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>! O <s>Hari</s>! Salutation to you, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! ||37||
O Lord of the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> [fig tree]! O one adorned with peacock-feathers! O one whose limbs are anointed with fine sandalwood!
O Lord of the groves of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>)! O one dark as a row of shining blue lotuses!
O beloved of <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>)! O joy of <s>Nanda</s>! O supreme-bliss-lotus-eyed one!

children.text: śrī-govinda mukunda sundara-tano māṃ dīnam ānandaya ||38||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Govinda</s>! <s>Mukunda</s>! O one of beautiful form! Delight me, the wretched one! ||38||

body.translated_text: The greatness of the stories of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> (<s>Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-kathā-māhātmya</s>):

children.translated_text: Even the teachings of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, when heard,
are far from the nectar of the narrative of <s>Hari</s>,
in which there are no melting of consciousness —
trembling, tears, horripilation, and so forth. ||39||
I do not seek the enjoyment of divine happiness,
nor do I desire liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), O Lord.
May they enter my ears day after day —
the nectars of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s playful deeds. ||40||
Ah! Day by day, the [evil of the] age of <s>Kali</s> is not dispelled,
yet the nectar-stream of ambrosia [flows] at every step.
Day by day, the fame of the son of <s>Yaśodā</s> is sung —
cool as sandalwood and the moon. ||41||
In the great ocean of nectar
of the youthful <s>līlā</s> (pastimes) of the son of <s>Nanda</s> —
for us who are immersed [therein],
what use is the salt water of <s>nirvāṇa</s>? ||42||
Sporting in the ocean
of the nectar of your stories, with great delight,
certain blessed ones make
the four goals of life seem like [worthless] straw. ||43||
There is the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the <s>Yamunā</s> is there,
the <s>Godāvarī</s> is there, the <s>Sarasvatī</s> too.
All the sacred fords (<s>tīrthas</s>) dwell there
where there is discourse on the noble stories of <s>Acyuta</s>. ||44||
That which is the fortune of enjoyment (<s>bhukti-lakṣmī</s>) on earth for the lustful,
that which is the fortune of liberation (<s>mukti-lakṣmī</s>) in the hearts of yogins,
that which is the fortune of bliss (<s>ānanda-lakṣmī</s>) of the crest-jewel among connoisseurs —
may that certain indescribable <s>līlā</s> of <s>Mādhava</s> [shine forth]. ||45||
Of the beauty of a full-blown blue lotus, moon-faced, dear to the peacock-feather crest,
bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, wearing the noble <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, in beautiful yellow garments,
his body worshipped by the lotus-eyes of the <s>gopīs</s>, surrounded by herds of cows and companies of cowherds —
I worship <s>Govinda</s>, absorbed in playing the sweet flute, adorned with divine ornaments. ||46||

body.text: śrī-śāradākārasya || [KK 3.82; KṛṣṇaS 106 (p49fn) attributed to Mṛtyu-sañjaya-tantra; ibid. HBV 3.114 (sāradā-tilake ca). In RKAD to Svāyambhuvāgama.]
body.translated_text: Of <s>Śrī Śāradākara</s>: [<s>KK</s> 3.82; <s>KṛṣṇaS</s> 106 (p49fn) attributed to <s>Mṛtyu-sañjaya-tantra</s>; ibid. <s>HBV</s> 3.114 (<s>sāradā-tilake ca</s>). In <s>RKAD</s> to <s>Svāyambhuvāgama</s>.]

children.translated_text: Bearing a left earring hanging from his shoulder, with delicately raised brow-creepers,
with slightly curved, tender lower lip, with a sidelong, spreading glance,
filling the flute with joy through his swaying finger-tendrils —
one should meditate at the root of the wish-fulfilling tree on him, graceful in three-fold bending posture, the enchanter of the world. ||47||
With the flute placed upon his lip,
with a <s>campaka</s> flower fashioned as a crest-ornament,
bending his left shoulder,
I constantly bow to him who has conquered <s>Kaṃsa</s>. ||48||
With lotus-feet crossed, with the charm of a graceful triple-bending posture,
with locks of hair loosened from the shoulder,
with a peacock-feather crest, holding the bamboo flute to his chest —
I approach him, the one of artless enchantment, for his special grace. ||49||

body.translated_text: Now, [on the Lord's] affection for devotees (<s>bhakta-vātsalya</s>):

children.translated_text: With hand extended, dismissing the untiring army-commander, rejecting
the fine jeweled sandals — why has he forgotten the inner palace?
Mounting <s>Garuḍa</s>, the king of birds, without the [usual] ceremony of invitation,
to the trumpeting of the chief elephant — homage to the haste of the <s>Bhagavān</s>! ||50||

body.translated_text: The words of <s>Śrī Draupadī</s> [seeking] her rescue:

children.translated_text: Like the sun rising in darkness, like a raft for the drowning
who have no boat, like a sweet rain-cloud for the thirsty,
like a treasure for the destitute, like a physician

children.text: bhiṣag iva kuśalaṃ no dātum āyāti śauriḥ ||51||
children.translated_text: for those afflicted with intense suffering — <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) comes to grant us well-being! ||51||

body.translated_text: Now, the greatness of his devotees:

children.translated_text: To <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>,
<s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, <s>Śaunaka</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Dālbhya</s>,
<s>Rukmāṅgada</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and others —
to these blessed supreme devotees (<s>paramabhāgavatas</s>) I bow. ||52||

children.text: śrī-viṣṇoḥ śravaṇe parīkṣid abhavad vaiyāsakiḥ kīrtane
children.translated_text: <s>Parīkṣit</s> excelled in hearing [of] <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>; <s>Vaiyāsaki</s> (<s>Śuka</s>) in glorification;

children.text: prahlādaḥ smaraṇe tad-aṅghri-bhajane lakṣmīḥ pṛthuḥ pūjane |
children.translated_text: <s>Prahlāda</s> in remembrance; <s>Lakṣmī</s> in serving his feet; <s>Pṛthu</s> in worship;

children.text: akrūras tv abhivandane kapi-patir dāsye 'tha sakhye 'rjunaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s> in salutation; the lord of monkeys (<s>Hanumān</s>) in servitude; and <s>Arjuna</s> in friendship.

children.text: sarvasvātma-nivedane balir abhūt kṛṣṇāptir eṣāṃ parā ||53||
children.translated_text: In complete self-surrender, <s>Bali</s> excelled — the supreme attainment of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was theirs. ||53||
Homage to them — experts in rescuing those
stuck in the aged mire of the ocean of existence,
those upon hearing the two syllables 'Kṛṣ-ṇa'
whose bliss arises with dancing body-hairs! ||54||
The blessed one whose mind is stilled by the joy of remembering <s>Hari</s>,
whose body has horripilation, whose eyes have tears of joy —
carry that foremost among men on the earth as long as moon and sun endure!
What use are those other burdens, [beings] going back and forth to <s>Yama</s>'s abode? ||55||

children.text: tvad-bhaktaḥ saritāṃ patiṃ culukavat khadyotavad bhāskaraṃ
children.translated_text: Your devotee sees the lord of rivers as a handful of water, the sun as a firefly,

children.text: meruṃ paśyati loṣṭravat kim aparaṃ bhūmeḥ patiṃ bhṛtyavat |
children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s> as a clod of earth, and moreover, the lord of the earth as a servant.
A heap of wish-fulfilling gems as a stone-fragment, a wish-fulfilling tree as a piece of wood,

children.text: saṃsāraṃ tṛṇa-rāśivat kim aparaṃ dehaṃ nijaṃ bhāravat ||56||
children.translated_text: <s>saṃsāra</s> as a pile of straw, and moreover, his own body as a mere burden. ||56||

children.text: mīmāṃsā-rajasā malīmasa-dṛśāṃ tāvan na dhīr īśvare
children.translated_text: For those whose vision is soiled by the dust of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, there is no thought of the Lord.
For those whose intellects are hardened by false arguments born of conceit, even talk of <s>Hari</s> is far away.

children.text: jānanto'pi na jānate śruti-sukhaṃ śrī-raṅgi-saṅgād ṛte
children.translated_text: Even those who know do not know the bliss of scripture without association with the devotees of <s>Śrī Raṅga</s>.

children.text: susvāduṃ pariveṣayanty api rasaṃ gurvī na darvī spṛśet ||57||
children.translated_text: Even though they serve the most delicious <s>rasa</s> (flavor), the heavy ladle does not taste it. ||57||
Some depend on knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>),
some depend on action (<s>karma</s>).
But we depend upon
the sandals of the feet of the servants of <s>Hari</s>. ||58||

body.translated_text: Now, the humble plea of the devotees (<s>dainyokti</s>):

children.text: nāmāni praṇayena te sukṛtināṃ tanvanti tuṇḍotsavaṃ
children.translated_text: Your names, lovingly uttered, create a festival of the mouth for the blessed;
your abodes, rain-cloud-dark, spread out as collyrium for the eyes.
The <s>sāman</s>-songs born from the flute adorn the dryness of the ears.

children.text: kāmānirvṛtacetasām api vibho nāśāpi naḥ śobhate ||59||
children.translated_text: [Yet for] us whose minds are not gratified, O Lord, even the very hope [of attaining you] is beautiful! ||59||
In the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, heavy with accumulated confusion,
seized by the crocodile of the profound three-fold suffering, crying from inner fear,
with the blazing <s>Sudarśana</s> [discus] that cuts the weariness of the gods —
now rescue, O <s>Hari</s>, this elephant-lord of my mind, bound by chains of anxiety! ||60||
In the mighty flood of existence, fathomless, with manifold afflictions laid bare,
as I sink far off, whirling with the force of delusion —
O friend of the shelterless, O moon of the moonlight of compassion!
Just once, without delay, give me the support of your hand! ||61||

children.text: nṛtyan vāyu-vighūrṇitaiḥ sva-viṭapair gāyann alīnāṃ rutair
children.translated_text: Dancing with its branches tossed by the wind, singing with the buzzing of bees,

children.text: muñcann aśru maranda-bindubhir alaṃ romāñcavān aṅkuraiḥ |
children.translated_text: shedding tears with drops of nectar, with horripilation through its shoots —

children.text: mākando'pi mukunda mūrcchati tava smṛtyā tu vṛndāvane
children.translated_text: even the mango tree, O <s>Mukunda</s>, swoons at the memory of you in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.

children.text: brūhi prāṇasamāna cetasi kathaṃ nāmāpi nāyāti te ||62||
children.translated_text: Tell me — how is it that your name does not even come to the mind [of me], who holds you equal to life? ||62||
That urgency which was [shown] in rescuing <s>Draupadī</s>,
that which was [shown] in the liberation of <s>Gajendra</s> (the lord of elephants) —
O embodiment of compassion, when I am in distress,
where has that urgency gone, O <s>Hari</s>? ||63||
Remembering your name 'Friend of the wretched' (<s>Dīnabandhu</s>),
O Lord of the <s>Yādavas</s>, though fallen, I take heart.
When your affection for devotees (<s>bhakta-vātsalatā</s>) is heard of,
my heart quickly trembles. ||64||
The four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others are your praisers;
<s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and others are your devotees, O Lord.
The hundred-faced one (<s>Indra</s>) and other gods are your servants.
O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, if [they are all these], then what are we? ||65||
There is none more supremely compassionate than you;
there is none more supremely wretched than I.
Having considered this, O <s>Hari</s>, toward me, a sinner —
do what is fitting, O Lord of the <s>Yadus</s>. ||66||
Beaten by hundreds of whips of the afflictions born of existence,
wandering in the treacherous by-paths of the senses —
restrain, O <s>Mādhava</s>, the horse of my mind
with the strong harness of devotion to your feet. ||67||

children.text: na dhyāto'si na kīrtito'si na manāg ārādhito'si prabho
children.translated_text: I have not meditated upon you, not glorified you, not worshipped you even slightly, O Lord;

children.text: no janmāntara-gocare tava padāmbhoje ca bhaktiḥ kṛtā |
children.translated_text: nor in the range of other births has devotion been offered at your lotus feet.
Therefore I have arrived at this state, becoming the vessel of much suffering.

children.text: tvaṃ kāruṇya-nidhe vidhehi karuṇāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa dīne mayi ||68||
children.translated_text: O treasury of compassion, show mercy, O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, to wretched me! ||68||
victory to you, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>!
Me, the perpetrator of endless heaps of sin —
devoid of refuge, O Lord of the World — protect, protect me! ||69||

body.translated_text: You are my refuge, O <s>Hari</s>, O Lord, O <s>Murāri</s>,

children.translated_text: At the beginning of the day, <s>Murāri</s>! At the beginning of the night, <s>Murāri</s>!
At the middle of the day, <s>Murāri</s>! At the middle of the night, <s>Murāri</s>!
At the end of the day, <s>Murāri</s>! At the end of the night, <s>Murāri</s>!

children.text: tvam eko gatir nas tvam eko gatir naḥ ||70||
children.translated_text: You alone are our refuge, you alone are our refuge! ||70||
fallen in the perilous ocean of existence.
By your grace, think of me
as like the dust at your lotus feet. ||71||

body.translated_text: O son of <s>Nanda</s>, I am your servant,

children.translated_text: We are not poets, nor logicians,
nor those who have entirely fathomed <s>Vedānta</s>.
We are not refuters of disputants — rather,
we are simply servants of the deceitful cowherd boy. ||72||
we are garrulous indeed, we do not care!
Maddened, supremely intoxicated by the wine of the <s>rasa</s> of <s>Hari</s>,
we roll on the ground, we dance, we revel! ||73||

body.translated_text: Let the people prattle as they wish —

children.text: nāhaṃ vipro na ca narapatir nāpi vaiśyo na śūdro
children.translated_text: I am not a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, nor a king, nor a <s>vaiśya</s>, nor a <s>śūdra</s>;

children.text: nāhaṃ varṇī na ca gṛhapatir no vanastho yatir vā |
children.translated_text: I am not a student (<s>varṇin</s>), nor a householder, nor a forest-dweller, nor a renunciant.
Rather, I am the servant of the servant of the servant
of the lotus feet of the husband of the <s>gopīs</s>, the ocean of surging, supreme, all-pervading, perfect bliss-nectar. ||74||
May that inner light shine in the hearts of the blessed, those who dwell in the freshly-verdant bowers of the best of mountains —
that reality of bliss (<s>satyānanda-rasa</s>), transcending the dominion of transformation!
But for us, may a certain cowherd, lustrous as a great sapphire,

children.text: gopaḥ ko'pi mahendra-nīla-ruciraś citte muhuḥ krīḍatu ||75||
children.translated_text: playful with the <s>rasa</s> of the love of the cowherd-women, longing for <s>Vṛndā</s>'s forest, play again and again in our hearts! ||75||
Let those devoted to poetic art praise <s>rasa</s>;
let those established in the crown of the <s>Vedas</s> [praise] the nectar of <s>Brahman</s>.
But we take refuge in a certain one adorned with a <s>guñjā</s>-berry crest,
who holds a flute. ||76||

children.text: dhyānātītaṃ kim api paramaṃ ye tu jānanti tattvaṃ
children.translated_text: Those who know a certain supreme truth beyond meditation —
let them have, in the cave of their hearts, the <s>Ātman</s> as pure consciousness alone.
But for us, our <s>Ātman</s> is this one — naturally sweet, with a smiling lotus-face,
dark as a rain-cloud, with a golden garment, lotus-eyed. ||77||

children.text: jātu prārthayate na pārthiva-padaṃ nendre pade modate
children.translated_text: He never seeks the status of a king, nor delights in the seat of <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: sandhatte na ca yoga-siddhiṣu dhiyaṃ mokṣaṃ ca nākāṅkṣati |
children.translated_text: he does not fix his mind on yogic attainments, nor does he desire liberation.
On the border of the <s>Kālindī</s>'s forest, [where stands] a steady lightning-[hued one], dark as a cloud — solely
in that pure <s>Brahman</s>, bound by the vine-arms of the cowherd women, the mind runs! ||78||

children.text: sandhyā-vandana bhadram astu bhavato bhoḥ snāna tubhyaṃ namo
children.translated_text: O twilight-prayer (<s>Sandhyāvandana</s>), may it be well with you! O ritual bath, salutations to you!

children.text: bho devāḥ pitaraś ca tarpaṇa-vidhau nāhaṃ kṣamaḥ kṣamyatām |
children.translated_text: O gods and ancestors, in the matter of offering libations — I am not able; forgive me!
Sitting down anywhere, [thinking of] the best of the <s>Yādava</s> clan, the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> —

children.text: smāraṃ smāram aghaṃ harāmi tad alaṃ manye kim anyena me ||79||
children.translated_text: remembering and remembering, I destroy my sins. I consider that sufficient — what need have I of anything else? ||79||
Let one become a servant of the son of <s>Devakī</s>;

children.text: yo bhavāni sa bhavāni kiṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: what of it, O <s>Bhavānī</s>?
On the wrong path or on the right path,
let the mind go wherever fate directs it! ||80||

children.text: mugdhaṃ māṃ nigadantu nīti-nipuṇā bhrāntaṃ muhur vaidikāḥ
children.translated_text: Let those skilled in worldly conduct call me a fool; let the <s>Vaidika</s>s repeatedly call me deluded;
let the crowd of relatives call me dull-witted; let my own brothers, with contempt for liberation, call me stupid —
The wealthy [call him] mad, the discerning [call him] lustful, the great hypocrite —

children.text: moktuṃ na kṣamate manāg api mano govinda-pāda-spṛhām ||81||
children.translated_text: [yet] the mind cannot abandon even slightly its longing for the feet of <s>Govinda</s>. ||81||
The dark form alone is the supreme form;
the best city is <s>Mathurāpurī</s>;
the age of adolescence (<s>kaiśoraka</s>) is to be meditated upon;
the primal <s>rasa</s> alone is the supreme <s>rasa</s>. ||82||
Let liberation shine forth before [me];
let the kingdom of renunciation reign here long —
[yet] of the lord of the cowherd boys,
service alone do I desire. ||83||
Sovereignty over the earth or utter destitution —
you give always either great honor or dishonor;
residence in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> or dwelling in hell —

children.text: hā vāsudeva mama nāsti gatis tvad-anyā ||84||
children.translated_text: alas, O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, I have no refuge other than you! ||84||
Let him grant sovereignty,
or let him bestow the three kinds of suffering —
whether happy or miserable,
may <s>Keśava</s> never abandon me! ||85||

body.translated_text: Now, the prayer of devotees filled with longing:

children.translated_text: From the lotus feet of <s>Nandanandana</s> (the son of Nanda),
the flowing drops of nectar —
oceans of the wealth of supreme bliss —
may they delight my heart unceasingly! ||86||
'Here he grazed the calves,'
'here our lord played the flute' —
thus weeping, as I speak,
may the day pass on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>! ||87||
In the bower-garden of devoted contemplation,
with yellow garment draped upon the hips,
delighting in the sweet cooing of the flute —
may my mind be [fixed] upon the deity of the <s>kadamba</s> tree! ||88||
With reddish, long eyes, delightful to the sight,
bearing a form lovely as ten million <s>Kandarpa</s>s (Cupids),
may he, who dwells in the lotus of my heart,
the sovereign of the urbane maidens of <s>Vṛndāṭavī</s>, appear to me today! ||89||
A flood of the nectar of charm,
the ripening of waves of sweetness,
the heart of [all] compassions —
may the deceptive youth shine forth! ||90||
May [my] births be there
where your sweet flute-melody
comes as a draught to the ears —
what need have I of talk of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? ||91||

children.text: āsvādyaṃ pramadārada-cchadam iva śravyaṃ navaṃ jalpitaṃ
children.translated_text: Savored like the lip of a woman half-opened, heard as fresh speech,
seen like a young woman's beauty and the splendor of loveliness,
proclaimed like the message of a woman long separated [from her lover] —

children.text: naivedyaṃ caritaṃ ca rūpam aniśaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa nāmāstu me ||92||
children.translated_text: may your conduct and form be my offering, and may your name, O Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, always be mine! ||92||
Eyes [streaming] with a flow of falling tears,
face [choked] with a voice obstructed by stammering,
body covered with goosebumps — when
will [my body] become thus upon uttering your name? ||93||

body.text: na dhanaṃ na janaṃ na sundarīṃ

children.translated_text: nor even poetry do I desire, O lord of the universe.
In birth after birth, O Lord,
may I have causeless devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) unto you! ||94||

body.translated_text: Neither wealth, nor followers, nor a beautiful woman,

children.translated_text: The fresh rain-cloud on the slope of <s>Govardhana</s>,
the fresh blue lotus of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>),
the generous <s>tamāla</s> tree of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> —
may it bring freshness to the three afflictions! ||95||
With playful, beautiful sidelong glances, deft in the art of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (Cupid's) <s>rasa</s>,
with the luster of swinging shark-shaped earrings flashing on his cheeks,
eager for the round-dance (<s>rāsa</s>) with the hosts of charming maidens of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: sa me sapadi mānase sphuratu ko'pi gopālakaḥ ||96||
children.translated_text: may some mysterious cowherd boy flash forth in my mind! ||96||

body.translated_text: Now, the longing of the devotees:

children.translated_text: The <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) are [worthless] like chaff —
what shall we now gather here?
The supreme <s>Brahman</s> was already seized
by the cowherd women (<s>Ābhīrīs</s>) with their eyes. ||97||
And who indeed would now believe it?
In the bower of the daughter of the cow-lord (<s>Yamunā</s>),
the <s>Brahman</s> sports with the cowherd women! ||98||

body.translated_text: To whom can I speak of it?

children.translated_text: I have studied logic (<s>Kāṇabhuja</s>); I have mastered philosophy (<s>Ānvīkṣikī</s>); I have been instructed in

children.text: mīmāṃsā viditaiva sāṅkhya-saraṇir yoge vitīrṇā matiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>; the path of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> is well-known; my intellect has crossed the [ocean of] <s>Yoga</s>;

children.text: vedāntāṃ pariśīlitāḥ sarabhasaṃ kiṃ tu sphuran-mādhurī-
children.translated_text: I have thoroughly examined the <s>Vedāntas</s> — yet, some sparkling stream
of sweetness from the flute of <s>Nanda</s>'s son draws my mind! ||99||
Of the sweetness of the nectar from the mouths of celestial women,
some wave of the arts' cleverness —
it agitates my mind,
the succession of the flute-sounds of <s>Murāri</s>! ||100||

children.text: apaharati mano me ko'py ayaṃ kṛṣṇa-cauraḥ
children.translated_text: He steals my mind — this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-thief!
Thief of the sins of those who bow; thief of <s>Pūtanā</s>'s life;
thief of the bangles and garments of the young <s>gopīs</s>;
thief of the eyes and hearts of the good people who behold him! ||101||
Enough of talk of heaven! Why speak of universal sovereignty?
Let the fortune of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) remain far away!
In the depth of the bowers on the bank of <s>Kalinda</s>'s daughter (<s>Yamunā</s>),
only the dark radiance, blue as a fresh <s>tamāla</s> tree, steals the mind. ||102||
Glanced at, smiled upon,
embraced with passion by the women —
in the bower of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
let us bow to that heap of emeralds! ||103||
When shall I see the boy of <s>Nanda</s>,
wearing a garland of <s>nīpa</s> flowers,
the protector of all beings,
with a shining <s>tilaka</s> on his forehead? ||104||
When in the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s>, hallowed by the company of the daughter of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>),
wandering again and again, [recounting] the waves of the deeds of the lord of <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: lapann uccair uccair nayana-payasāṃ veṇibhir ahaṃ
children.translated_text: speaking aloud again and again, with streams of tears from my eyes,
shall I, with longing, abundantly water the trees? ||105||
On a height hard to ascend, [that sound] placing its foot, [a foot] rich in fortune, even for goddesses,
dances upon the topknot — the stiff [abode] of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>;
the sound born of the flute, holding sweetness, that [sound] of the foe of <s>Madhu</s> —
suddenly it ascends the crest of our hearing! ||106||
'Here was the home of <s>Nanda</s>; here the shattering of the cart occurred;
he who breaks all bonds was himself bound here with ropes — <s>Dāmodara</s>!'
Thus drinking the stream of nectar flowing from the mouths of the elders of <s>Mathurā</s>,

children.text: ānandāśrudharaḥ kadā madhupurīṃ dhanyaś cariṣyāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: when, fortunate, with tears of joy, shall I wander through <s>Madhupurī</s>? ||

body.text: (Quoted in BRS 1.3.40 - yathā padyāvalyām, but not found in this edition)
body.translated_text: (Quoted in BRS 1.3.40 — as from the <s>Padyāvalī</s>, but not found in this edition)

children.translated_text: With the beautiful splendor of a fully bloomed peacock feather,
his lotus-face resting on his mother's breast,
moving the tips of his lotus-feet —
when will <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> come into the path of my eyes? ||107||
<s>Bhakti</s> is service to the Blessed Lord;
<s>Mukti</s> is the transgression of his feet.
What fool, having attained the state of a servant,
would desire the state of a sovereign? ||110||
For that [liberation] which cuts the bonds of worldly existence,
I have no longing —
[not when] 'You are the master, I am the servant'
— that [relationship] would be dissolved thereby. ||111||
Alas, wonder strikes [me], O friend —
remembering those [devotees], my mind [is stirred].
Even the discerning would develop
a craving for the absolute dissolution [that is devotion]! ||112||

children.text: kā tvaṃ muktir upāgatāsmi bhavatī kasmād akasmād iha
children.translated_text: 'Who are you?' 'I am liberation (<s>Mukti</s>), come to you.' 'Why have you come here unbidden?'
'By the remembrance of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O lord, I have been brought to the rank of a maidservant.'

children.text: dūre tiṣṭha manāg anāgasi katha kuryād anāryaṃ mayi
children.translated_text: 'Stand far away! Do not come near — lest you, guiltless as you are, commit an ignoble act against me:'
'from the fragrance of you, the application of the sandal-paste of his own name might be erased!' ||113||

body.translated_text: Now, the truth of the doctrine of the Blessed Lord:

children.text: arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīr guruṣu nara-matir vaiṣṇave jāti-buddhir
children.translated_text: Regarding the sacred image of <s>Viṣṇu</s> as mere stone; regarding the <s>guru</s> as a mere man; regarding a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> by caste-identity;
regarding the foot-water of <s>Viṣṇu</s> or the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, which destroys the impurity of <s>Kali</s>, as [mere] water;
regarding the name-<s>mantra</s> of Śrī <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which removes all sin, as an ordinary word;

children.text: viṣṇau sarveśvareśe tad-itara-sama-dhīr yasya vā nārakī saḥ ||114||
children.translated_text: regarding <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of all lords, as equal to others — whoever [thinks] thus is destined for hell! ||114||

children.text: hatyāṃ hanti yad-aṅghri-saṅga-tulasī steyaṃ ca toyaṃ pador
children.translated_text: His foot-<s>tulasī</s> destroys murder; the water of his feet [destroys] theft;
his food-offering [destroys] the sin of excessive drinking; [it destroys] the [sin] born of union with the <s>guru</s>'s wife;
the mind devoted to Śrī <s>Śādhina</s> (Hari), association with <s>Hari</s>'s devotees — the sin born of that [false] association —
the glory of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone and <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> is beyond this world! ||115||

body.translated_text: Now, the prayer at the offering of <s>naivedya</s> (food offering):

children.translated_text: In the soft rice of the brāhmaṇa women, in <s>Vidura</s>'s food, in the curd of the cows of <s>Vraja</s>,
in the butter and flattened rice of a friend, O foe of <s>Mura</s>,
in the breast-milk of <s>Yaśodā</s>, in the honey offered by the <s>Vraja</s>-maidens —

children.text: yathāsīd āmodas tam imam upahāre'pi kurutām ||116||
children.translated_text: whatever delight was yours therein, may you have that same delight in this offering too! ||116||

children.text: yā prītir vidurārpite muraripo kunty-arpite yādṛśī
children.translated_text: Whatever love [there was] in that offered by <s>Vidura</s>, O foe of <s>Mura</s>, and how it was in that offered by <s>Kuntī</s>,

children.text: yā govardhana-mūrdhni yā ca pṛthuke stane yaśodārpite |
children.translated_text: that which was [felt] on the summit of <s>Govardhana</s>, that in the flattened rice, that in the breast of <s>Yaśodā</s>,
that in the offering of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, that given by <s>Śabarī</s>, that on the lips of the women,

children.text: yā vā te muni-bhāminī-vinihite'nne'trāpi tām arpaye ||117||
children.translated_text: that in the food placed by the wives of the sages — that [love] I too offer here! ||117||
In the milk offered by <s>Śyāmalā</s>, in the sugar-candy distributed by <s>Kamalā</s>,

children.text: datte laḍḍūni bhadrayā madhurase sobhābhayā lambhite |
children.translated_text: in the <s>lāḍḍu</s> given by <s>Bhadrā</s>, in the sweet juice obtained from <s>Śobhābhayā</s> —

children.text: tuṣṭiryā bhavatas tataḥ śataguṇāṃ rādhā-nideśān mayā
children.translated_text: whatever satisfaction you had — a hundredfold more than that, by <s>Rādhā</s>'s command,

children.text: naste'smin puratas tvam arpaya hare ramyopahāre ratim ||118||
children.translated_text: in this excellent offering placed before you, O <s>Hari</s>, bestow your delight! ||118||

children.text: he mātur mathure tvam eva niyataṃ dhanyāsi bhūmī-tale
children.translated_text: O mother <s>Mathurā</s>! You alone are truly blessed upon this earth!

children.text: nirvyājaṃ natayaḥ śataṃ savidhayas tubhyaṃ sadā santu naḥ |
children.translated_text: May a hundred sincere salutations be always ours, close by your side!

children.text: hitvā hanta nitāntam adbhuta-guṇaṃ vaikuṇṭham utkaṇṭhayā
children.translated_text: Abandoning, alas, the supremely wondrous <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, with longing,

children.text: tvayy ambhoja-vilocanaḥ sa bhagavān yenāvatīrṇo hariḥ ||119||
children.translated_text: in you, the Blessed Lord <s>Hari</s>, the lotus-eyed one, has descended! ||119||
'Here was the home of <s>Nanda</s>; here the shattering of the cart occurred;
he who breaks all bonds was himself bound here with ropes — <s>Dāmodara</s>!'
Thus drinking the stream of nectar flowing from the mouths of the elders of <s>Mathurā</s>,

children.text: nāndāśru-dharaḥ kadā madhu-purīṃ dhanyaś cariṣyāmy aham ||120||
children.translated_text: when, fortunate, with tears of joy, shall I wander through <s>Madhupurī</s>? ||120||
Where even the primordial teacher, the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>,
was born as a pillar, without desiring [anything] —
adorned with the splendor of feet marked with discus, banner, and goad —
that <s>Mathurā</s>, the royal capital of <s>Hari</s>, shines today! ||121||
The seed of the tree of liberation, the deliverer rescuing [one] from the multitude of calamities,
the abode of the <s>rasa</s> of divine love, the carrier of the burden of desire, the one who carries across —
where, for its residents, the twofold function of the consciousness-power (<s>cicchakti</s>) arises —

children.text: mathnātu vyasanāni māthura-purī sā vaḥ śriyaṃ ca kriyāt ||122||
children.translated_text: may that city of <s>Mathurā</s> destroy [your] miseries and bestow upon you splendor! ||122||
The foe of <s>Mura</s>, your lord, bestows
that which he never gives to the devotee who worships him —
yet you bestow this <s>bhaktiyoga</s>!
O <s>Mathurā</s>, your glory is beyond the reach of words! ||123||
<s>Mathurā</s> in hearing, <s>Mathurā</s> in sight,
<s>Mathurā</s> on the lips, <s>Mathurā</s> in the heart,
<s>Mathurā</s> before, <s>Mathurā</s> behind —
sweet, sweet, <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Mathurā</s>! ||124||
You worship <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>);

children.text: tvam api haraṃ tvaṃ ca tat-paraṃ brahma |
children.translated_text: you too [worship] <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); and you, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> beyond him —
[but] as for me, in whom the bliss of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is established,
I praise the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s>! ||125||
let others, afraid of worldly existence, resort to the <s>Mahābhārata</s> —
I praise <s>Nanda</s>,
in whose courtyard the supreme <s>Brahman</s> [crawls]! ||126||

body.translated_text: Let others resort to the <s>Śruti</s>; others to the <s>Smṛti</s>;

children.translated_text: Clad in garments red as the <s>bandhūka</s> flower,
with a beautiful topknot, his eyes captivated by <s>Mukunda</s>,
I praise <s>Nanda</s>, whose body is stout,
whose complexion is fair as sandalwood. ||127||
She who has the lotus-naveled one (<s>Padmanābha</s>) on her lap,
who has the luster of a fresh rain-cloud, with a wondrous array of radiance,
who has brought about the delight of the world —
I repeatedly bow to <s>Yaśodā</s>. ||128||
His hands and feet exceedingly red,
with a charming <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow pigment) <s>tilaka</s> mark,
who stubbornly overturned the cart (<s>śakaṭa</s>),
I praise <s>Murāri</s> lying on his back. ||129||
With eyes half-opened, drinking fully from one breast,
with his hand wiping the other breast freshly flowing with milk,
while his mother playfully moves her finger in his mouth and he repeatedly smiles —
may the radiance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s teeth, white as the great splendor of drops of milk, protect you! ||130||
His eyes rolling at the "phūt" sounds made by the queen of the cowherds (<s>Yaśodā</s>),
crawling on both knees across the ground,
with lips sweet as the nectar of a fresh smile —
I worship that certain child, dark as a <s>tamāla</s> leaf. ||131||
"Where is the face? Where is the eye? Where is the nose?
Where is the ear? Where is the topknot?" — thus instructed,
placing his petal-like fingers here and there on each,
the Lord delighted the community of cowherd women. ||132||
"Just now your body was bathed
and anointed with unguents,
and just now already, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
your body is covered with dust!" ||133||
Five years old, exceedingly restless, running
about in the courtyard with eyes veiled by curls,
adorned with tinkling bells, bracelets, necklace, and anklets —
bow to the delightful son of <s>Nanda</s>! ||134||

children.text: adhara-madhure kaṇṭhaṃ kaṇṭhe sacāṭu dṛśau dṛśor
children.translated_text: Placing his sweet lips on a lip, his neck on a neck, with coaxing his eyes on eyes,
his forehead on a forehead, with the <s>gopī</s> women in great agitation,

children.text: śiśur iti rudan kṛṣṇo vakṣaḥ-sthale nihitaś cirān
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, crying "I am just a child!" was held long upon their bosoms,
his hair standing on end in secret, smiling — may he whose form is languid with desire protect us! ||135||
"O mother of his, we shall tell of your son's deeds, for he has assumed the guise of extreme infancy —
how he is a delight to the eyes of the doe-eyed women in the mountain caves!"
Thus addressed, under the pretense of licking, placing a finger on his own mouth,

children.text: gopībhiḥ purataḥ punātu jagatīm uttāna-supto hariḥ ||136||
children.translated_text: may <s>Hari</s>, lying on his back before the <s>gopī</s>s, purify the world! ||136||
<s>Vanamālin</s> (the garlanded one), on his father's lap,
performs acts befitting childhood,
while ever-new smiles of the young cowherd women
blossom forth in succession. ||137||
"How much fresh butter have you taken?"
— thus <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was asked by <s>Yaśodā</s>,
"Only this much!" — and in the presence of the elders
he held up <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>'s breast. ||138||

children.text: kva yāsi nanu caurike pramuṣitaṃ sphuṭaṃ dṛśyate
children.translated_text: "Where are you going, little thief? The stolen goods are clearly visible!

children.text: dvitīyam iha māmakaṃ vahasi kañcuke kandukam |
children.translated_text: You carry a second ball of mine inside your garment!"
Forcibly kneading the breast-pair of the young <s>gopī</s> who said "Let go!" —
all glory to <s>Keśava</s> in <s>Gokula</s>, his body bristling with radiant horripilation! ||139||
Having spotted a vessel of fresh butter from afar,
crawling on his knees with great eagerness,
his face turned back in fear of his mother —
I worship <s>Keśava</s>'s ineffable infancy! ||140||
While stealing fresh butter, seeing his own reflection emerge in a nearby jeweled pillar,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mugdhatayā kumāram aparaṃ sañcintayan śaṅkayā |
children.translated_text: and in his innocence imagining it to be another boy, with suspicion —

children.text: man-mitraṃ hi bhavān mayātra bhavato bhāgaḥ samaḥ kalpito
children.translated_text: "You are my friend! I have allotted you an equal share here,

children.text: mā māṃ sūcaya sūcayety anunayan bālo hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||141||
children.translated_text: don't report me, don't report me!" — thus coaxing, may the child <s>Hari</s> protect you! ||141||
Awakened at dawn by the sounds of churning curds,
he entered the house of the cowherd women with silent steps,
quickly blowing out the lamps with the breeze from his lotus-mouth —
may child <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having devoured the fresh butter, protect me! || 142 ||
Holding in his left hand the string of tinkling bells with their sound restrained,
stooping down, moving softly on tiptoe, gently laughing,
with glances keeping at bay the smiling women who faced him —

children.text: mātuḥ paścād aharata harir jātu haiyaṅgavīnam || 143 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> once stole the fresh butter from behind his mother! || 143 ||
Taking three or four steps on the ground near the doorway,
casting his pair of eyes restlessly in all directions,
wearing a clear smile, his mind eager for the sport of stealing curds —
<s>Madhuripu</s> (the foe of <s>Madhu</s>) enters the house of the <s>gopī</s>s with apprehension. || 144 ||
Rubbing his smooth, fragrant lips from the theft of milk and such, wiping them with his hands,
sniffing his hand again and again, then roughly rubbing the belt of tinkling bells,

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ viśāle diśi diśi vikiran locane lolatāre
children.translated_text: casting his wide, restless eyes again and again in every direction —

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ jananyāḥ parisaram ayate kūṭa-gopāla-bālaḥ || 145 ||
children.translated_text: the deceitful cowherd boy slowly, slowly approaches the vicinity of his mother. || 145 ||

children.text: śambho svāgatam āsyatām ita ito vāmena padmodbhava
children.translated_text: "O <s>Śambhu</s>, welcome! Please sit here. O <s>Padmodbhava</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), on the left.

children.text: krauñcāre kuśalaṃ sukhaṃ surapate vitteśa no dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: O slayer of <s>Krauñca</s> (<s>Skanda</s>), are you well? O lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>), are you happy? O lord of wealth (<s>Kubera</s>), you haven't been seen!"

children.text: itthaṃ svapna-gatasya kaiṭabha-ripoḥ śrutvā jananyā giraḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing such words of the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) spoken in his sleep, his mother said,

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ bālaka jalpasīty anucitaṃ thūthūt-kṛtaṃ pātu vaḥ ||146||
children.translated_text: "What what are you babbling, child?" — may that absurd sputtering protect you! ||146||

children.text: dhīrā dharitri bhāva bhāram avehi śāntaṃ
children.translated_text: "Be patient, O Earth! Know that your burden shall be relieved,
for I shall cast down the wretch <s>Kaṃsa</s>!"
— such sleep-utterances of the child of <s>Vasudeva</s>,
heard by the cowherd women who stood amazed, are glorious! ||147||

body.translated_text: Now, astonishing the parents, instruction, and so forth —

children.text: kālindī-puline mayā na na mayā śīlopaśalye na na
children.translated_text: "On the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s>? By me? No, no! By me? At the bed of good conduct? No, no!

children.text: nyagrodhasya tale mayā na na mayā rādhā-pituḥ prāṅgane |
children.translated_text: At the foot of the banyan tree? By me? No, no! By me? In the courtyard of <s>Rādhā</s>'s father?"

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇa itīrite saniyamaṃ gopair yaśodā-pater
children.translated_text: When told "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has been seen" by the cowherds with restraint, as <s>Yaśodā</s>'s husband

children.text: vismerasya puro hasan nija-gṛhān niryan hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||148||
children.translated_text: stood astonished before them, <s>Hari</s>, laughing, going out from his own house — may he protect you! ||148||
"Child, when wandering in the remote mountain caves where the cows roam far,

children.text: hiṃsrān vīkṣya puraḥ purāṇa-puruṣaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ dhyāsyasi |
children.translated_text: upon seeing ferocious beasts, you should meditate on the ancient person, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!"

children.text: ity uktasya yaśodayā murāripor avyāj jaganti sphurad-
children.translated_text: When thus instructed by <s>Yaśodā</s>, the artless smile of <s>Murāri</s> that flashed forth
from the firm pressing together of both <s>bimba</s>-red lips — that smile with its hidden meaning! ||149||

children.text: rāmo nāma babhūva huṃ tad abalā sīteti huṃ tāṃ pitur
children.translated_text: "There was one named <s>Rāma</s>" — "Hmm." — "And that woman, <s>Sītā</s>" — "Hmm." — "While she and her father's
son dwelt in <s>Pañcavaṭī</s> forest, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> abducted her."
Hearing this ancient tale of his own, narrated by his mother, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> cried:

children.text: saumitre kva dhanur dhanur dhanur iti vyagrā giraḥ pāntu vaḥ ||150||
children.translated_text: "<s>Saumitre</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>)! Where is the bow? The bow! The bow!" — may those agitated words protect you! ||150||

children.text: śyāmoccandrā svapiti na śiśo naiti mām amba nidrā
children.translated_text: "The dark moon has risen high, O child, sleep! Mother, sleep does not come to me.

children.text: nidrāhetoḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ kām apūrvāṃ kuruṣva |
children.translated_text: For the sake of sleep, listen — shall I tell some wondrous tale?"

children.text: vyaktaḥ stambhān naraharir abhūd dānavaṃ dārayiṣyann
children.translated_text: "<s>Narahari</s> (man-lion) clearly burst forth from the pillar, about to tear apart the demon" —
upon saying this, a smile arises on the face of the son of <s>Devakī</s>! ||151||

body.translated_text: Now, the pastimes of cow-herding and so forth —

children.translated_text: O Lord! With your arm placed on the head of a staff resting on one leg,
singing songs of bull-fights, with a head-ornament fashioned from flowers,
deeply engaged in the art of combat between two proud great bulls —
may <s>Murāri</s> in his form of the playful cowherd, assuming the pastime of cow-herding, protect us! ||152||
While the cowherds, intoxicated by the sweet sound of the flute,
drink in <s>Mukunda</s> with all their eyes barely moving — alas! —
meanwhile the cows, greedy for mouthfuls of tender grass, have gone far away
into the valley-hollows of <s>Govardhana</s> mountain. ||153||

body.translated_text: Now, the excellence of the <s>gopī</s>s' love |

children.translated_text: Composure (in the <s>gopī</s>s) means clinging to the garment on their hips even while taking <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s name;
discrimination means seeking a secluded place when beginning love-play;
virtuous conduct means seeking the husband's house when ceasing from amorous sport;
and all such restraints are guarded only until the sound of <s>Murāri</s>'s flute is heard. ||154||
Beholding <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the beautiful-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>
wished that all their senses were nothing but eyes;
and hearing the melodious strains of his flute,
they wished again that all were nothing but ears. ||155||
The young women sporting playfully in the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>, having wrapped themselves in thin silk garments,
emerged and, having wrung the water from their limbs, looked in all directions,
while <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) watched secretly for a long time from a bower of creepers meeting near the bank —

children.text: śaureḥ sambhramayann imā vijayate sākūta-veṇur dhvaniḥ ||156||
children.translated_text: all glory to the purposeful sound of his flute that agitates them! ||156||
From the trembling that arose in the bud of his lotus-hand drenched with perspiration,
he did not notice the flute slipping onto the top of his lotus-feet;
his heart captivated by the playfully swaying cowherd women in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> —
all glory to the vacant breath of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> in his three-bent form! ||157||

body.translated_text: The question of <s>Rādhā</s> upon first seeing <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.translated_text: His face beautiful with the art of dancing eyebrows,
with <s>kaṅkellī</s> (Ashoka) buds adorning his ear-ornaments,
"Who is this one, resembling a fresh touchstone in appearance,
who with the sound of his flute, O friend, renders me helpless?" ||158||
His splendor deep as the interior of a blue lotus,
wearing a garment resembling a cluster of molten gold,
his chest adorned with a captivating pearl necklace —
"Who is this youth who makes the entire world pervaded by <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love)?" ||159||
"There is a certain one who suckles at the breast of darkness (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the dark one);
he sings with slightly curved steps.

children.text: yan manāg api niśamya kā vadhūr
children.translated_text: What woman, hearing even a little of this,
is not shaken to the core of her heart?" || 160 ||
As if revealing through bodily transformations
the affliction of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Cupid's) arrows that dwelt in her mind,
<s>Rādhā</s>, with a sorrowful face, then spoke
these words before her circle of friends: ||161||
"Ever since in the bower by the <s>Yamunā</s>
a certain one with the luster of a dark cloud was beheld,
like water on a lotus leaf,
since then, my heart trembles." ||162||

children.text: akasmād ekasmin pathi sakhi mayā yāmuna-taṭaṃ
children.translated_text: "Unexpectedly, on a certain path, O friend, while I was going to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
I saw one whose body was dark as a fresh rain-cloud.

children.text: sa dṛg-bhaṅgyā kiṃ vākuruta na hi jāne tata idaṃ
children.translated_text: What he did with a glance of his eyes, I do not know — but since then

children.text: mano me vyālolaṃ kvacana gṛhakṛtyo na lagate ||163||
children.translated_text: my mind is restless; no household duty appeals to me." ||163||
First, a blue radiance; then the fragrance of musk;
then the playful sound of a flute, followed by the sweet jingling of a girdle;
then a wave of astonishment entwined like a streak of lightning —

children.text: taraṅgāl lāvaṇyaṃ tad anu sahajānanda udagāt ||164||
children.translated_text: then <s>lāvaṇya</s> (beauty), and then arose spontaneous bliss. ||164||
"Today, O beautiful one, on the bower-ground by the bank of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>),
that lover of sport,
playing the flute again and again,
<s>Mādhava</s> steals my heart!" ||165||
Ever since, in the <s>vānīra</s>-bower on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
the playful feet of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> were beheld by my eyes,
since then my mind, even in the slightest task,

children.text: na hi lagati muhūrtaṃ kiṃ vidheyaṃ na jāne ||166||
children.translated_text: does not settle for even a moment — I know not what to do! ||166||
Ever since the moon-face of the joy of the <s>Yadus</s>
came within the range of [my] eyes, O companion,
since then, whether in the Malaya breeze or in fire,
my mind has turned away from its natural discernment. ||167||
How unbecoming! How unbecoming!
How unbecoming is this that has befallen [me]!
Thinking him [merely] a cowherd boy,
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s> — <s>Hari</s> was gazed upon out of curiosity! ||168||
The mouth dries up, the pair of thighs
grows numb, the heart trembles,
the cheeks perspire — O friend,
has the one garlanded with forest-flowers (<s>Vanamālī</s>) been seen? ||169||
Above the <s>tamāla</s> tree, O friend,
there is some [radiant being] like the full autumnal moon-disk.
And there, the warbling of a flute
drags the family honor downward. ||170||
Alas! Even him, the beloved, my mind desires to see —
that mind which, on his account, is no longer virtuous.
O moon-faced one, the moon, the gentle breeze,
and sandalwood — they all only spread my agony! ||171||
The reproach of the elders, the infamy,
and the harsh conduct of the husband — all of it,
the flute of the foe of <s>Mura</s>
makes one forget entirely! O <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>! ||172||
Wealth, home, children — all these,
and friends, and noble birth —
[matter only] so long as the one garlanded with forest-flowers (<s>Vanamālī</s>), by the <s>Yamunā</s>,
does not make the eyes dance! ||173||

body.text:
tṛpyantu me chidram avāpya śatravaḥ
karotu me śāsti-bharaṃ gṛheśvaraḥ |
maṇis tu vakṣoruha-madhya-bhūṣaṇaṃ
mamāstu vṛndāvana-kṛṣṇa-candramā || 174 || kasyacit |
body.translated_text: Let my enemies gloat, finding an opening! Let the master of the house heap his punishments upon me! But may the jewel, the ornament amidst my breasts, be the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-moon of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>! ||174|| By an unknown author:

body.text:
svāmī nihantu vihasantu puraḥ sapatnyo
bhartur bhajantu guravaḥ pitaraś ca lajjām |
etāvatā yadi kalaṅki kulaṃ tathāstu
rāmānuje mama tanotu mano'nurāgam ||175|| kasyacit |
body.translated_text: Let the master punish me; let the co-wives laugh before me; let the elders and parents of the husband bear shame! If by this much the family is stained — so be it! May the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) spread affection in my mind! ||175|| By an unknown author:

children.text: svāmī kupyati kupyatāṃ parijanā nindanti nindantu mām,
children.translated_text: The master is angry — let him be angry! The servants slander — let them slander me!

children.text: anyat kiṃ prathatām ayaṃ ca jagati prauḍho mamopadravaḥ |
children.translated_text: What else is to be proclaimed? Let this my bold misconduct spread through the world!

children.text: āśāsyaṃ punar etad eva yad idaṃ cakṣuś ciraṃ vardhatāṃ
children.translated_text: But this alone is to be wished for: may these eyes long flourish,
by which the body of the foe of <s>Mura</s>, the essence of beauty, is drunk in! ||176||
What use, O messenger, is my hard-to-fulfill heart's desire?
Alas, by whom were so many meritorious deeds performed?
This much alone is the fruit of my birth: that <s>Murāri</s>
bestows his comings and goings upon the path of my eyes. ||177||
O friend, for me who am struck by fate,
let the fortune of seeing him be or not be!
But if that sound of the flute
should fall upon the path of the ear — that alone is enough! ||178||
O star-guided [moon], O fourth-night crescent,
O increaser of the ocean of love — to you, O deity,

children.text: argho namo bhavatu me saha tena yūnā
children.translated_text: this <s>arghya</s> (offering-water) and salutation be! Along with that youth,
even by false defamatory words, may the fulfillment of pride be [mine]! ||179||

body.translated_text: Now, the speculation of another clever friend (<s>sakhī</s>):

children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> does not deliberate about anything;
she merely makes the eyes whirl about.
O friend, it is understood — she is possessed
by the spirit of the <s>kadamba</s>-tree deity! ||180||
Granted, the body is horripilated, the eyes hold tears,
the words falter with broken syllables, O friend, the breast trembles.
We know — the sweetness of <s>Mukunda</s>'s flute-music
makes your mind restless, O moon-faced one! ||181||
The vow of the chaste wife has gone; well-known indeed are those various words [of censure].

children.text: tathāpi taralāśaye na vimatāsi ko durgrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Yet, O restless-hearted one, you are not dismayed — what a stubborn resolve!
O friend, what shall I do? When the flute-melody of the foe of the <s>Dānavas</s> is heard,

children.text: manāg api mano na me sumukhi dhairyam ālambate ||182||
children.translated_text: not even slightly does my mind, O fair-faced one, hold fast to composure. ||182||
Let my infamy be — that aside;
but tell me the truth:
What was the state of your mind
when you heard the flute-music of <s>Hari</s>? ||183||

children.text: satyaṃ jalpasi duḥsahāḥ khala-giraḥ satyaṃ kulaṃ nirmalaṃ
children.translated_text: True, the words of malicious folk are unbearable; true, the family is spotless;

children.text: satyaṃ niṣkaruṇo'py ayaṃ sahacaraḥ satyaṃ sudūre sarit |
children.translated_text: true, this companion is pitiless; true, the river is very far.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ sakhi vismarāmi jhaṭiti śrotrātithir jāyate
children.translated_text: All that, O friend, I forget instantly — if the rising melody
of the enchanting, sweet flute of the maddening <s>Mukunda</s> becomes a guest of the ear! ||184||

body.translated_text: Now, the friend's playful consolation to <s>Rādhā</s>:

children.translated_text: The night is thick with clouds, the world is hidden in the womb of darkness;

children.text: dvayas tava navaṃ navaṃ vapur apūrva-līlāmayam |
children.translated_text: your form, ever new, is filled with unprecedented play, O pair.

children.text: alaṃ sumukhi nidrayā vraja gṛhe'pi naktaṃ carī
children.translated_text: Enough of sleep, O fair-faced one! Go to [your] home, O night-wanderess!
The deity of the <s>kadamba</s> grove [awaits], dark as a fresh <s>tamāla</s> tree! ||185||
When she sees you among the fruits, she makes them dark as collyrium;
when she hears of you, she turns the ear-ornament into a blue lotus.
When she contemplates you in her heart, O full-moon-faced one,
she makes [of you] a fresh sapphire hidden at her breast. ||186||
She has accepted the betel-leaf, but the fair-faced one, at the words of her attendants,

children.text: smaraty antaḥśūnyā murahara gatāyām api niśi |
children.translated_text: does not remember — empty within — even when the night has passed, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>.
Her hand remains just so, holding the betel-vine shoot,
and her mouth just so, accustomed to the splitting of the areca-nut. ||187||
Her limbs licked by the fire of <s>prema</s> (divine love),
<s>Rādhā</s>, O Lord of the World,
has slipped from her bed to the ground,
yet is unable to return to it. ||188||
O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, the weight of [your] recklessness —
how can it be described — toward the fawn-eyed one?
Even though fallen into an ocean of grief,
she does not abandon the sweetness of love for you. ||189||
she plays upon the <s>vīṇā</s>,
she teaches the parrot in the cage
the syllables of your message — <s>Rādhā</s>! ||190||

body.translated_text: She sings in songs, she celebrates in flute-music,

children.translated_text: How many lotus-eyed cowherd-women, skilled in the arts of amorous play,
are there not in the town of <s>Murāri</s>!

children.text: rādhe tvayā mahad akāri tapo yad eṣa
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhā</s>, great is the <s>tapas</s> (austerity) you have performed, that this
<s>Dāmodara</s> has supreme, utmost love for you! ||191||

children.text: vatsān na cārayati vādayate na veṇum
children.translated_text: He does not tend the calves, he does not play the flute,
he does not delight in the <s>Yamunā</s>-forest breeze.
Concealed in the bower, with head listlessly turned,
the son of <s>Nanda</s> sighs within, O beautiful one, [thinking of] you. ||192||

body.text:
sarvādhikaḥ sakala-keli-kalā-vidagdhaḥ
snigdhaḥ sa eṣa mura-śatrur anargha-rūpaḥ |
tvāṃ yācate yadi bhaja vraja-nāgari tvaṃ
sādhyaṃ kim anyad adhikaṃ bhuvane bhavatyāḥ ||193|| rāṅgasya ||
body.translated_text: He is the foremost of all, skilled in all arts of amorous play, tender, this foe of <s>Mura</s>, of priceless beauty. If he implores you, then accept him, O belle of <s>Vraja</s>! What greater object is to be attained by you in the world? ||193|| By <s>Rāṅga</s>:

children.translated_text: Place your feet softly; put on the dark-blue
garment; hide the row of bangles with the end of your shawl.
Do not speak, O bold one! The rays of your teeth,
bright as the autumnal moon, will dispel the darkness! ||194||
'Has the path — dangerous as the coils of an angry she-serpent — been crossed?
Have the many harsh words of the family guardians been endured?'
Thus remembering again and again, the lotus-eyed one
casts a reddened sidelong glance toward the quarter of the slightly-dimmed moonlight. ||195||
[She who is] frightened at night even of a serpent carved in a picture —

children.text: kiṃ vā brūmas tvad-abhisaraṇe sāhasaṃ mādhavāsyāḥ |
children.translated_text: what shall we say of the boldness of this <s>Mādhava</s>'s [beloved] in going to meet you?
As <s>Rādhā</s> was going through the darkness, in utmost secrecy, terrified of her own radiance [revealing her],
her hand was placed [over] the crest-jewel of the serpent-hood on the path [to conceal its glow]! ||196||
To <s>Acyuta</s>, who is churned by the god of love,
say something with a beaming smile!
And sprinkle, O fawn-eyed one,
[him] with cascading waterfalls of nectar from the gestures of your eyes! ||197||
You yourself, O lotus-eyed one, blinded by love,
made the offering of your beautiful body to <s>Govinda</s>, O friend.
Do not now be miserly in granting a sidelong glance!
When the elephant has been sold, what is the dispute about the goad? ||198||

body.translated_text: By an unknown author: (BRS 2.4.114; <s>Bhaktirasāyana</s>; DKK; MSN 5.15)

children.translated_text: Then, by <s>Rādhā</s>, who was absorbed in the utmost love,
whose feelings blossomed with the art of embrace,
together with her, he celebrated the festival of homage to the god of love —
he who wears the crest of peacock-plumes. ||199||

children.text: asmin kuñje vināpi pracalati pavanaṃ vartate ko'pi nūnaṃ
children.translated_text: 'In this bower, even without any wind stirring, there is certainly someone present!

children.text: paśyāmaḥ kiṃ na gatvety anusarati gaṇe bhīta-bhīte'rbhakāṇām |
children.translated_text: Shall we not go and see?' — thus, in the troop of frightened children [who said this],

children.text: tasmin rādhāsakho vaḥ sukhayatu vilasan krīḍayā kaiṭabhārir
children.translated_text: may that friend of <s>Rādhā</s>, the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, delight you, playfully sporting,
producing terrible, fierce roars like a mighty lion's growls. ||200||

body.text: atha krīḍānantaraṃ tatra jānatīnāṃ sakhīnāṃ narmoktiḥ
body.translated_text: Now, after the love-play: the playful words of the knowing friends (<s>sakhīs</s>) there:

children.translated_text: 'Here, in the midst of the <s>nicūla</s>-bower, in the heart of the playground of the Lover,
whose is this lonely bed made of fresh sprouts?'

children.text: iti nigadati vṛnde yoṣitāṃ pāntu yuṣmān
children.translated_text: When <s>Vṛndā</s> speaks thus among the women — may the glances,
dappled with smiles, exchanged between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> protect you! ||201||

body.translated_text: Now, the words of an innocent child:

children.text: kṛṣṇa tvad-vanamālayā saha kṛtaṃ kenāpi kuñjāntare
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, someone in the bower has made this [thing]

children.text: gopī-kuntala-barha-dāma tad idaṃ prāptaṃ mayā gṛhyatām |
children.translated_text: with your forest garland and the <s>gopī</s>'s hair and peacock-feather cord — I found it, take it!'
When thus told by the milk-mouthed cowherd child, may the glances of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> triumph —
turned aside with embarrassment, languid, and curved with gentle smiles! ||202||

body.text: atha rādhayā saha dināntare keliḥ tatra sakhī-vākyam
body.translated_text: Now, sport with <s>Rādhā</s> on another day; therein, the friend's words:

children.translated_text: 'Now, why do you go on churning the yogurt,
O you with languid limbs heavy with amorous exertion?
O pot-breasted one, [he] awaits you lovingly in the bower —'
so [coos] the soft warbling of <s>Murāri</s>'s flute! ||203||
'The mother-in-law is the divinity of [reading] every gesture of the eyes; the sisters-in-law are spying;
the husband is jealous even of a sigh; the co-wives are eager to smell out [any hint of infidelity].

children.text: tad-dūrād ayam añjaliḥ kim adhunā dṛgbhaṅgi-bhāvena te
children.translated_text: Therefore, from afar, this salutation [is all I can offer]. What now, with your art of sidelong glances?
O connoisseur of the various compositions of amorous skill — this effort here is in vain!' ||204||
As the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> makes the calls of the cuckoo and such birds into signals,
and he keeps hearing the jingling of conch-shell bangles eager to unlock the door,
and his spirit is wounded by the bold old crone's words: 'Who is this? Who is this?' —
the night passed, [with him] in the hollow of a <s>koli</s> (<s>jujube</s>) tree in the corner of <s>Rādhā</s>'s courtyard! ||205||

children.text: āhūtādya mayotsave niśi gṛhaṃ śūnyaṃ vimucyāgatā
children.translated_text: '[She has been] invited today to the festival; she has left the house empty and come at night;

children.text: kṣīvaḥ preṣyajanaḥ kathaṃ kulavadhūr ekākinī yāsyati |
children.translated_text: the servant is drunk — how will a respectable wife go home alone?

children.text: vatsa tvaṃ tad imāṃ nayālayam iti śrutvā yaśodā-giro
children.translated_text: My boy, you then — escort her home!' Hearing <s>Yaśodā</s>'s words,
the sweetly smiling, languid glances of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> are victorious! ||206||

children.text: gacchāmy acyuta darśanena bhavataḥ kiṃ tṛptir utpadyate
children.translated_text: 'I am leaving, O <s>Acyuta</s> — is there satisfaction from merely seeing you?

children.text: kiṃ tv evaṃ vijana-sthayor hata-janaḥ sambhāvayaty anyathā |
children.translated_text: But if we two remain thus in a secluded spot, the wicked folk will imagine the worst.'
Thus, clasping the <s>gopī</s> whose farewell-gesture hinted at the distress of a pretended departure [she didn't really wish to make],

children.text: āśliṣyan pulakotkarāñcita-tanur gopīṃ hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||207||
children.translated_text: may <s>Hari</s>, his body bristling with horripilation, protect you! ||207||

body.translated_text: Now, the jest of the friend (<s>sakhī-narma</s>):

children.translated_text: O friend, with horripilation, trembling,
you have arrived home from the outdoors.
Surely you have been disturbed
by the serpent <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O blessed one! ||208||

body.text: atha punar anyedyur abhisārikā tatra sakhī-vākyam |
body.translated_text: Now, on another day, the words of a friend to the <s>abhisārikā</s> (a woman going to a tryst):

children.translated_text: Adorning his locks with unfading spring flowers, he
plays within the bowers, O wagtail-eyed one, the one with bower-like glances.

children.text: asmān mandira-karmatas tava karau nādyāpi viśrāmyataḥ
children.translated_text: The household duties have not yet released your hands today.

children.text: kiṃ brūmo rasaikāgraṇīr asi ghaṭī neyaṃ vilamba-kṣamā ||209 ||
children.translated_text: What can we say — you are the foremost in <s>rasa</s>; this moment is not to be wasted! ||209||

body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>'s words to a friend who is testing her:

children.translated_text: Is it modesty that has opened [this path]? Why then does the door remain bolted, bound by family honor?

children.text: maryādaiva vilaṅghitā pathi punaḥ keyaṃ kalindātmajā |
children.translated_text: Is it propriety that has been violated? Then what is this <s>Kālindī</s> (river) again on the path?

children.text: ākṣiptā khala-dṛṣṭir eva sahasā vyālāvalī kīdṛśī
children.translated_text: Has the wicked glance been cast? Suddenly — what sort of line of serpents is this?

children.text: prāṇā eva samarpitāḥ sakhi ciraṃ tasmai kim eṣā tanuḥ ||210||
