children.translated_text: My very life-breaths have been surrendered to him for so long, O friend — what then is this body? ||210||
After two or three steps, [she drops] the play-lotus; after three or four, the jasmine garland from her braids;

children.text: kaṇṭhān mauktika-mālikāṃ tad anu ca tyaktvā padaiḥ pañcamaiḥ |
children.translated_text: from the neck, the pearl necklace; and then, after the fifth step —
the slender-limbed one, churning inwardly with love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, eager for the distant tryst,

children.text: tanvaṅgī nirupāyam adhvani paraṃ śreṇībharaṃ nindati || 211 ||
children.translated_text: helplessly curses the weight of her girdle-chain on the path. ||211||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>vāsaka-sajjā</s> (a woman preparing for her lover's arrival):

children.translated_text: 'Prepare the bed, O messenger, with tender shoots in the bower of inner creepers!'

children.text: nirbandhaṃ mama puṣpa-maṇḍana-vidhau nādyāpi kiṃ muñcati |
children.translated_text: 'Won't the insistence on flower-adornment release me even now?'
'Look — playfully, the dense darkness has spread over <s>Vṛndā</s>'s forest.'

children.text: tad gopendra-kumāram atra milita-prāyaṃ manaḥ śaṅkate ||212||
children.translated_text: 'My heart suspects that the son of the chief cowherd is about to arrive here!' ||212||

children.text: sakhi sa vijito vīṇā-vādyaiḥ kayāpy apara-striyā
children.translated_text: 'O friend, he has been conquered by the <s>vīṇā</s>-playing of some other woman.'

children.text: paṇitam abhavat tābhyāṃ tava kṣapā-lalitaṃ dhruvam |
children.translated_text: 'The wager between those two must have been your night of dalliance.'
'For how else, even when the <s>śephālikā</s> flowers are falling,
and the moon has risen to the middle of the sky, is the beloved still delayed?' ||213||

children.text: aratir iyam upaiti māṃ na nidrā
children.translated_text: This weariness does not leave me; sleep does not come.

children.text: gaṇayati tasya guṇān mano na doṣān |
children.translated_text: My mind counts his virtues, not his faults.
The night does not cease its longing for union.
The body wastes away, but not the passion. ||214||
'Arise, O messenger! Let us go, let us go!'
'The <s>yāma</s> (night-watch) has passed, yet he has not come.'
'She who could live
even beyond this — her life-lord must indeed be [hers]!' ||215||
A lac-mark on the forehead, the imprint of a bracelet all over the neck,
kohl-blackness on the face, deep <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel-leaf) stain on the eyes —

children.text: dṛṣṭā kopa-vidhāyi maṇḍanam idaṃ prātaś ciraṃ preyaso
children.translated_text: seeing this anger-provoking adornment on the beloved in the morning, for a long time,
the sighs of the doe-eyed one, [gazing at] the lotus of his playful chest, came to an end. ||216||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the woman whose lover has been unfaithful):

body.text: autkalasya || (Amaru 71/60; SKM 2.24.4; Spd 3740, Sbhv 2215; Smv 82.17; Daśarūpaka 2.6)

children.text: kṛtaṃ mithyā-jalpair virama viditaṃ kāmuka cirāt
children.translated_text: 'Enough with these false protestations! Desist — I have known for long, O lover!

children.text: priyāṃ tām evoccair abhisara yadīyair nakha-padaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Go worship that very beloved of yours, by whose nail-marks

children.text: vilāsaiś ca prāptaṃ tava hṛdi padaṃ raga-bahulair
children.translated_text: and many-hued coquetries she has gained a place in your heart.

children.text: mayā kiṃ te kṛtyaṃ dhruvam akuṭilācāra-parayā ||217||
children.translated_text: What use have you for me, who am devoted to nothing but honest conduct?' ||217||
'Together with your hundred desires, O rogue, that very sweetheart of yours
remains in your mind — charming through feigned affection.

children.text: asmākam asti na hi kaścid ihāvakāśas
children.translated_text: For us there is surely no room here;
therefore, enough with this mockery of falling at [our] feet!' ||218||
'Even unadorned, O <s>Mādhava</s>,
you always forcibly steal my heart.
Why are you not adorned
now — with her nail-scratches?' ||219||

body.translated_text: The words of her who has attained despondence through betrayal (<s>khaṇḍanā</s>):

children.translated_text: 'The endeavors are past; the honor of love has dissolved;

children.text: durāśā yātā me pariṇatir iyaṃ prāṇitum api |
children.translated_text: hope has left me; this transformation — even to keep breathing —
let the stimuli (<s>vibhāvas</s>) of separation, famed for the slaughter of the love-lorn, act as they please upon me —
the cuckoo, the springtime, the moon, and all the rest.' ||220||
'O five-arrowed one (<s>Pañcaśara</s>, Love), do not release your five arrows at this body!
O Wind, do not sprinkle it with the dense flow of honey-nectar!
These limbs, condemned by the breaking of his love —
my life-breath today is unable to cling to them in any way.' ||221||
that certain one, skilled in deception —
display your pride (<s>māna</s>) toward the slayer of <s>Mura</s>!
For with a man who has many beloveds,
graciousness (<s>dākṣiṇya</s>) only brings suffering.' ||222||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>māninī</s> (the woman displaying amorous anger):

children.text: bhavatu viditaṃ chadmālāpair alaṃ priya gamyatāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Enough! Your deceitful words are understood. Go, O beloved!

children.text: tanur api na te doṣo'smākaṃ vidhis tu parāṅmukhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The fault is not yours but ours — fate has turned against us.

children.text: tava yathā tathābhūtaṃ prema prapannam imāṃ daśāṃ
children.translated_text: Your love, such as it was, has arrived at this state.

children.text: prakṛti-capale kā naḥ pīḍā gate hata-jīvite || 223 ||
children.translated_text: O fickle one by nature, what pain [can there be] for us, now that [our] life is destroyed?' ||223||

children.text: kas tvaṃ tāsu yadṛcchayā kitava yās tiṣṭhanti gopāṅganāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Who are you to those <s>gopī</s> women who stand there by chance, O cheat?

children.text: premāṇaṃ na vidanti yās tava hare kiṃ tāsu te kaitavam |
children.translated_text: They do not know your love, O <s>Hari</s> — what trickery have you with them?

children.text: eṣā hanta hatāśayā yad abhavaṃ tvayy ekatānā paraṃ
children.translated_text: Alas, wretched am I, for I alone was singularly devoted to you —

children.text: tenāsyāḥ praṇayo'dhunā khalu mama prāṇaiḥ samaṃ yāsyati || 224 ||
children.translated_text: and so, this love of hers will now surely depart along with her life-breaths.' ||224||
'Why do you gaze at him with averted neck?
Let him go, let him go, O friend — the slayer of <s>Pūtanā</s>!
Let him serve that wicked woman, skilled in perverse ways,
as if she were the supreme deity!' ||225||

children.text: premāvagāhana-kṛte mānaṃ mā kuru cirāya karabhoru |
children.translated_text: 'Do not sustain your pride too long for the sake of deepening love, O plantain-thighed one!

children.text: nākarṇi kiṃ nu mugdhe jātaṃ pīyūṣa-manthane garalam ||226||
children.translated_text: Have you not heard, O innocent one, that poison arose during the churning of nectar?' ||226||

children.text: vidhumukhi vimukhībhāvaṃ bhāvini mad-bhāṣaṇe mā gāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O moon-faced one, O emotional one, do not turn away from my speech!
O foolish one — the one hidden by scripture is met only through some [rare] good fortune.' ||227||
'Enough, enough with the name of that merciless one!

children.text: punar api saiva katha gataḥ sa kālaḥ |
children.translated_text: Again the same story — that time is past.',
'Speak on, speak on, even so, O messenger —
a reply is owed even to an enemy.' ||228||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (woman separated by a quarrel):
Words of a sympathetic friend (<s>dakṣiṇa-sakhī</s>) to her:

children.translated_text: 'Without considering the outcome of love, without heeding your friends,

children.text: tvayākāṇḍe mānaḥ kim iti sarale preyasi kṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: you suddenly displayed pride toward your beloved — why, O guileless one?
These embers, blazing with the flames of the fire of separation,
have been drawn by your own hand — so enough now with weeping in the wilderness!' ||229||

body.text: amaroḥ || (Amaru 112/80; Sbhv 1170; SKM 2.42.1, Smv 56.9, Srk 659 Vikaṭanitambā)

body.translated_text: Now, the words of a harsh friend (<s>karkaśa-sakhī</s>):

children.translated_text: 'Loosening the bonds of pride all around,
do not squander your dignity, O <s>Gaurī</s>!
The foe of the <s>Dānavas</s> does not practice honesty —
sincerity is not appropriate toward a deceiver!' ||230||

children.text: bhrū-bhaṅgo guṇitaś ciraṃ nayanayor abhyastam āmīlanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The frown has been practiced long; the half-closing of the eyes has been rehearsed;

children.text: roddhuṃ śikṣitam ādareṇa hasitaṃ maune'bhiyogaḥ kṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: laughter has been carefully trained to be restrained; an effort at silence has been made.

children.text: dhairyaṃ kartum api sthirīkṛtam idaṃ cetaḥ kathañcin mayā
children.translated_text: To summon courage, this heart has been somehow steadied by me;

children.text: baddho māna-parigrahe parikaraḥ siddhis tu daive sthitā || 231 ||
children.translated_text: the apparatus for maintaining pride has been bound — but success rests with fate.' ||231||

body.text:
jānāmi maunam alasāñgi vaco-vibhaṅgīr
bhañgī-śataṃ nayanayor api cāturīṃ ca |
ābhīra-nandana-mukhāmbuja-saṅga-śaṃsī
vaṃśīravo yadi na mām avaśīkaroti ||232|| kasyacit ||
body.translated_text: 'I know the silence; I know the languorous arts of speech, the hundred coquetries of the eyes, and the cleverness too. But if the sound of the flute, which proclaims union with the lotus-face of the son of <s>Ābhīra</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), does not overpower me [then I can maintain my resolve].' ||232|| Of someone:

children.translated_text: 'Truly I hear, O friend, that he is ever-fickle with new loves,
that cowherd — yet even so, the Love-god torments my heart.
Even when, by some stratagem, composure is achieved [regarding] him,
his flute of time devours me.' ||233||

body.translated_text: Of the revered Lord's (<s>Śrī Mat Prabhu</s>, i.e., <s>Caitanya</s>):

children.translated_text: 'I do not know — when the beloved comes before [me],
and speaks sweet words, O dear one —
do my limbs become
all ears, or all eyes?' ||234||

children.text: murāriṃ paśyantyāḥ sakhi sakalam aṅgaṃ na nayanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'For her who beholds <s>Murāri</s>, O friend, every limb becomes an eye;
for her who hears the multitude of <s>Hari</s>'s virtues, [every limb] is piled up as an ear;

children.text: samaṃ tenālāpaṃ sapadi racayantyā mukham ayaṃ
children.translated_text: for her who at once engages in conversation with him, [every limb] becomes a mouth —
this sweetness of the Creator's arrangement is not [easily grasped].' ||235||
'You are pure and guileless,
while the flute-faced one is crooked in three ways.',
'A crooked one is easily [won over] —
so it is the <s>vaijayantī</s> garland [that adorns] his chest, O friend!' ||236||

children.text: niḥśvāsā vadanaṃ dahanti hṛdayaṃ nirmūlam unmathyate
children.translated_text: 'Sighs burn the face, the heart is uprooted and churned,

children.text: nidrā neti na dṛśyate priyamukhaṃ rātrindivaṃ rudyate |
children.translated_text: sleep does not come, the beloved's face is not seen, I weep day and night,

children.text: aṅgaṃ śoṣam upaiti pāda-patitaḥ preyāṃs tathopekṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: the body wastes away, the beloved has fallen at my feet yet I have ignored him —

children.text: sakhyaḥ kaṃ guṇam ākalayya dayite mānaṃ vayaṃ kāritāḥ ||237||
children.translated_text: O friends, considering what virtue [in pride], have we been made to assume this pride toward the beloved?' ||237||

body.text: mānaja-viraheṇa dhyāyantīṃ tāṃ prati kasyāścid vākyam |
body.translated_text: Someone's words to her who meditates in separation born of pride:

children.translated_text: 'Abstinence from food, supreme withdrawal from the entire realm of sense-objects,

children.text: nāsāgre nayanaṃ yad etad aparaṃ yac caikatānaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: the eye fixed on the tip of the nose, and moreover the mind one-pointed,

children.text: maunaṃ cedam idaṃ ca śūnyam akhilaṃ yad viśvam ābhāti te
children.translated_text: this silence, and this — the entire universe appears empty to you.',

children.text: tad brūyāḥ sakhi yoginī kim asi bhoḥ kiṃ viyoginy api ||238||
children.translated_text: 'So tell us, O friend — are you a yoginī, or are you [just] a woman in separation?' ||238||
'When given the choice between union and separation,

children.text: varam iha viraho na tu saṅgamas tasya |
children.translated_text: separation here is better than union with him.',
'In union, he is but one;
in separation, the three worlds are pervaded by him.' ||239||

children.text: sañjāte virahe kayāpi hṛdaye sandānite cintayā
children.translated_text: 'When separation has arisen, when the heart has been somehow chained by longing,
when one sits in the dense shade of the reed-forest on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> —
may the songs of the cowherd, the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, sprinkle [us] — the melodies of the <s>kalakaṇṭha</s> (cuckoo's) cooing,
sounded through the breath forced from the palate, [the flute] deprived of [its own] tongue.' ||240||

children.text: śiraś chāyāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ svayam akṛta rādhā-caraṇayor
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself cast his head as a shadow at <s>Rādhā</s>'s feet;
she too [cast] the shadow of her vine-like arms upon his image.',

children.text: iti krīḍā-kope nibhṛtam ubhayor apy anunaya-
children.translated_text: 'Thus in their love-quarrel, secretly, the conciliations and favors of both —

children.text: prasādau jīyās tām api guru-samakṣaṃ sthitavatoḥ ||241||
children.translated_text: may they be victorious! — [were exchanged] even while standing before their elders.' ||241||
'She is entirely dyed [with love], [her] passion —
like the <s>guñjā</s> berry, she does not display it on her face.
The redness of your words
is only on the mouth — like a parrot's.' ||242||
'O handsome one, by your settling in her heart, even in the blazing fire of <s>Smara</s> (Love),
the excess of love has long been revealed.',

children.text: tava tu hṛdaye śīte'py evaṃ sadaiva sukhāptaye
children.translated_text: 'But in your heart, even when cool, for the attainment of happiness always —

children.text: mama sahacarī sā niḥsnehā manāg api na sthitā ||243||
children.translated_text: my companion, she, stands not even slightly without affection.' ||243||

body.translated_text: Now, the news of the next day (<s>dināntara-vārtā</s>):

children.translated_text: 'Having arrived, with the friend appeased by prostrations granting an opening, the rogue [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], though guilty,
secretly at the bedside, performs a body-massage freely.',

children.text: jñātvā sparśa-vaśāt tayā kila sakhī-bhrānty eva vakṣaḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Perceiving by touch that she, under the delusion of [thinking him] a friend, slowly [opens her] chest —'
Saying "You are tired," with eyes closed, he was joyfully lifted up. ||244||
But in truth, out of fear of her elders, by her,
when the bud of feigned <s>māna</s> (jealous sulking) was displayed,
<s>Hari</s>, informed by the glance of a clever dear friend,
went to the bower of creepers on the riverbank. ||245||
<s>Mādhava</s>, in the arbor of sweet <s>mādhavī</s> creepers,
where bees were buzzing loudly,
sang with his flute, beautiful to the ears,
which was a fishhook for the fish of the <s>gopī</s>s' <s>māna</s> (jealous pride). ||246||

body.translated_text: These two are by certain [poets]. (UN 10.64, RSAK 1.100f)

body.text: puṣpa-cchalena kṛṣṇam anveṣayantīṃ rādhāṃ prati kasyāścid uktiḥ |
body.translated_text: Words of a certain woman to <s>Rādhā</s> who was searching for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> under the pretext of gathering flowers:

children.translated_text: May your path be auspicious — abandon any thought of obstacles!
O beautiful one, this much has been observed by me along the waterway of my eyes:
In the water, a blue lotus of brilliant qualities; on the bank, an ornament of <s>tamāla</s> trees;
in the grove, some male <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> mountain is playing. ||247||

body.text: tatra yamunā-tīre gatayā rādhayā saha saṃkathā |
body.translated_text: Here, a conversation with <s>Rādhā</s> who has gone to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>:

children.text: kā tvaṃ mādhava-dūtikā vadasi kiṃ mānaṃ jahīti priye
children.translated_text: "Who are you? A messenger of <s>Mādhava</s>? What are you saying — 'Abandon your <s>māna</s> (sulking), O beloved'?

children.text: dhūrtaḥ so'nyamanā manāg api sakhi tvayy ādaraṃ nojjhati |
children.translated_text: That rogue is fickle-minded, yet, O friend, he does not abandon his regard for you even slightly."
Thus, having led <s>Rādhā</s>, delighted by the relish of mutual conversation, to the bower-house, disguised as a <s>sakhī</s> (girlfriend),

children.text: nītvā kuñja-gṛhaṃ prakāśitatanuḥ smero hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||248||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, having revealed his true form, smiling — may he protect you! ||248||

body.text:
vasantaḥ sannaddho vipinam ajanaṃ tvaṃ ca taruṇī
sphurat-kāmāveśe vayasi vayam apy āhita-padāḥ |
vraja tvaṃ vā rādhe kṣaṇam atha vilambasva yadi vā
sphuṭaṃ jātas tāvac catura-vacanānām avasaraḥ ||249|| kasyacit ||
body.translated_text: Spring has armed itself, the forest is unpeople, and you are a young woman in an age throbbing with the onset of desire, and we too have taken our positions. Go if you will, O <s>Rādhā</s>, or else linger for a moment — clearly, an occasion for clever words has arisen! ||249|| Of a certain [poet].

children.text: svāmī mugdhataro vanaṃ ghanam idaṃ bālāham ekākinī
children.translated_text: "My lord is most naive, this forest is dense, I am a young girl, alone,
a mass of darkness from shadows dark as <s>tamāla</s> trees covers the earth.

children.text: tan me sundara kṛṣṇa muñca sahasā vartmeti rādhā-giraḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, O handsome <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, quickly release my path!" — hearing these words of <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: śrutvā tāṃ parirabhya manmatha-kalāsakto hariḥ pātu vaḥ || 250 ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Hari</s>, who embraced her and became absorbed in the arts of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), protect you! ||250||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>svādhīna-bhartṛkā</s> (the heroine whose lover is under her control):

body.text:
makarī-viracana-bhaṅgyā
rādhā-kuca-kalasa-mardana-vyasanī |
ṛjum api rekhāṃ lumpan

children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> in the guise of a cowherd is victorious! ||251||
Of a certain [poet]. (Spd 77, of <s>Harihara</s>)

body.translated_text: With the pretense of fashioning <s>makarī</s> (crocodile) designs, addicted to kneading the pitcher-like breasts of <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: ete lakṣmaṇa jānakī-virahiṇaṃ māṃ khedayanty ambudā
children.translated_text: "O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, these rain clouds torment me, separated from <s>Jānakī</s>,

children.text: marmāṇīva ca ghaṭṭayanty alam amī krūrāḥ kadambānilāḥ |
children.translated_text: and these cruel <s>kadamba</s>-scented winds strike at my very vital points!"
Thus, he who was seen by <s>Rādhā</s> while murmuring of his separation in a former birth —

children.text: serṣyaṃ śaṅkitayā sa vaḥ sukhayatu svapnāyamāno hariḥ ||252||
children.translated_text: may that <s>Hari</s>, drowsing, watched with jealousy and suspicion by her, bring you happiness! ||252||

body.translated_text: Now, the stealing of the flute:

children.text: nīcair nyāsād atha caraṇayor nūpura mūkayantī
children.translated_text: Silencing her anklets by gently removing them from her feet,
repeatedly lifting and holding up the bangles and bracelets from her forearms,
with a startled expression, again and again glancing around,

children.text: smitvā smitvā harati muralīm aṅkato mādhavasya ||253||
children.translated_text: smiling repeatedly, she steals the flute from the lap of <s>Mādhava</s>. ||253||
"May your heart be without cracks, may it be full,
may your garrulousness cease, may you have gravity!
O friend, beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, I always offer you blessings,

children.text: yad vāsare murali me karuṇāṃ karoṣi ||254||
children.translated_text: if on that day, O flute, you show me mercy." ||254||

children.text: śūnyatvaṃ hṛdaye salāghavam idaṃ śuṣkatvam aṅgeṣu me
children.translated_text: "The emptiness in my heart, this lightness, the dryness in my limbs,
the garrulousness in speaking the name of the Lord of <s>Vraja</s> — you have given me your own nature!

children.text: tat kiṃ no murali prayaccasi pnar govinda-vaktrāsavaṃ
children.translated_text: Then why, O flute, do you not also give me the nectar of <s>Govinda</s>'s lips,

children.text: yaṃ pītvā bhuvanaṃ vaśe vidadhatī nirlajjam udgāyasi ||255||
children.translated_text: drinking which you hold the world in your power and sing shamelessly?" ||255||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Hari</s>'s return to <s>Vraja</s> in the evening:

children.translated_text: With his flute sounding low notes as the day wanes, driving the herds back to <s>Gokula</s>,
wearing on his head the <s>barhāpīḍa</s> (peacock-feather crest), grey with the dust of cow-hooves,
encircled by a wilting forest garland, weary yet beautiful in form,
may <s>Keśava</s>, a festival for the eyes of the cowherd women, bestow blessings upon you! ||256||

body.translated_text: Here, the words of a certain woman:

children.text: dṛṣṭyā keśava gopa-rāga-hatayā kiñcin na dṛṣṭaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: "O <s>Keśava</s>, with my sight destroyed by the passion of the cowherds, nothing at all was seen by me,

children.text: tenādya skhalitāsmi nātha patitāṃ kiṃ nāma nālambase |
children.translated_text: and so today I have stumbled — O lord, will you not support me who has fallen?

children.text: ekas tvaṃ viṣameṣu khinna-manasāṃ sarvābalānāṃ gatir
children.translated_text: You alone are the refuge of all helpless women whose hearts are distressed in times of difficulty."

children.text: gopyaivaṃ gaditaḥ saleśam avatād goṣṭhe harir vaś ciram || 257 ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by a <s>gopī</s>, with a slight smile — may <s>Hari</s> protect you in <s>Goṣṭha</s> (the cowherd settlement) for long! ||257||

body.text: kasyacit || (Dhvan, Vakro, SD 4.14; Smv 2.93; different kinds of vyaṅgya)
body.translated_text: Of a certain [poet]. (Dhvan, Vakro, SD 4.14; Smv 2.93; different kinds of vyaṅgya)

children.translated_text: With his flute placed at the region of his navel,
one lotus-hand resting on the tail of a cow,
his staff adorned by the other hand,
the lotus-eyed one arrived at <s>Vraja</s>. ||258||
Honored discreetly along the path by one woman with movements of her brow-creeper, by another with openings of her eyes,
by yet another with showers of smile-moonlight,
upon the face of <s>Rādhā</s>, which possesses the splendor of indifferent courtesy born of pride and distinction —
the glances of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, fallen with anxious supplication, are triumphant! ||259||
With neck turned sideways, ear-ornament touching the shoulder, with hair bound up and raised by a gleaming peacock feather,
with the play of slightly curved brow-creepers,
with lower lip pressed upon the sounding flute, with half-closed gaze cast meaningfully upon the face of <s>Rādhā</s> —

children.text: nyastāmīlita-dṛṣṭi gopa-vapuṣo viṣṇor mukhaṃ pātu vaḥ ||260||
children.translated_text: may the face of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of a cowherd protect you! ||260||
With flute-face resting against the cheek on the shoulder, lips engaged upon the pair of <s>bimba</s>-red lips of the flute,
producing a soft, gentle sound through the breath blown from both,
with slightly swaying, trembling clusters of necklaces, with fingers rising, dancing, and dipping upon each hole —
may the lord of <s>Rādhā</s> protect you! ||261||
With fingers controlled by the tip of his thumb, his feet placed firmly on the ground,
having thoroughly moistened the edge of her breast-cloth with drops of milk,
with the stream of milk falling into the mouth of the pail held between his lowered knees —

children.text: dhārādhvāna-manoharaṃ sakhi payo gāṃ dogdhi dāmodaraḥ || 262 ||
children.translated_text: charming with the sound of flowing streams, O friend, <s>Dāmodara</s> milks the cow! ||262||
From the deceitful one, upon suddenly hearing the tinkling of her girdle-gems,
he who was embracing her became slack in the knot of his arms.
"But where shall I tell this? Reeling from the poison of your many honeyed and buttery words,

children.text: viṣeṇāghūrṇantī kim api na sakhī me gaṇayati ||263||
children.translated_text: my friend takes no heed of anything." ||263||

body.translated_text: Of a certain [poet]. (Amaru 73/109, SD 3.37) The deceitful hero.

children.translated_text: Gazed at with terror by <s>Yaśodā</s>, with eyes full of love for his virtues by <s>Rādhā</s>,
by the clinging cowherd boys who eagerly honored his own strength with their exertions,
and strangely by <s>Nanda</s> with a mixture of fear, joy, and wonder —
may <s>Hari</s>, playfully holding the great mountain steady on his lotus-hand, protect you! ||264||

children.text: ekenaiva cirāya kṛṣṇa bhavatā govardhano'yaṃ dhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: "O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, you alone have held up this <s>Govardhana</s> for so long,

children.text: śrānto'si kṣaṇam āssva sāmpratam amī sarve vayaṃ dadhmahe |
children.translated_text: you are weary — rest for a moment, all of us together shall now bear it!"
When the group of cowherds thus raised their arms enthusiastically, and the mountain began to sink slightly from the bending of his arm,

children.text: nyañcac-chaila-bharārdite viruvati smero hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||265||
children.translated_text: and they cried out as they were crushed by the weight of the mountain — may <s>Hari</s>, smiling, protect you! ||265||
"You are weary — let go of the mountain,
we shall bear it!" — when they spoke thus, with arms gone slack,
as the cowherds were bent and spread out
under the burden, <s>Hari</s>, laughing, is victorious! ||266||

body.text:
dūraṃ dṛṣṭi-pathāt tirobhava harer govardhanaṃ vibhratas
tvayy āsakta-dṛśaḥ kṛśodari kara-srasto'sya mā bhūd ayam |
gopīnām iti jalpitaṃ kalayato rādhā-nirodhāśrayaṃ
śvāsāḥ śaila-bhara-śrama-bhrama-karāḥ kaṃsa-dviṣaḥ pāntu vaḥ || 267 || śubhāṅkasya | (SKM 1.60.4)
body.translated_text: "Go far from his line of sight, O <s>Rādhā</s>, while <s>Hari</s> holds up <s>Govardhana</s> — with his gaze fixed on you, O slender-waisted one, may this mountain not slip from his hand!" As the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> savors these words of the <s>gopī</s>s, which serve as a pretext for gazing at <s>Rādhā</s>, may his sighs — which create the illusion of exhaustion from the mountain's weight — protect you! ||267|| Of <s>Śubhāṅka</s>. (SKM 1.60.4)

children.translated_text: "Take us across the <s>Yamunā</s>!"
— thus repeatedly called out to by the <s>gopī</s>s with eager cries,
pretending to sleep lazily on the riverbank,
<s>Hari</s>, doubly languid, is victorious! ||268||

children.text: uttiṣṭhārāt tarau me taruṇi mama taroḥ śaktir ārohaṇe kā
children.translated_text: "Get up quickly! Ferry me across!" "O young woman, what power have I to climb my own boat?"

children.text: sākṣād ākhyāmi mugdhe taraṇim iha raver ākhyayā kā ratir me |
children.translated_text: "I'll tell you plainly, O naive girl — by the word 'taraṇi' (boat/sun), what pleasure is there for me?"

children.text: vārteyaṃ nau-prasaṅge katham api bhavitā nāvayoḥ saṅgamārthā
children.translated_text: "This talk of a boat-expedition will somehow result in a union of us two,"
"Even this is mere talk!" — with a smiling face, I worship the unconquered one who conquered the mountain, through <s>Rādhā</s>! ||269||
"Released by the mass of waves, the daughter of the sun —

children.text: navyā ca naur iti vacas tava tathyam eva |
children.translated_text: and a new boat — your words are indeed true.
But this itself is my excessive cause for apprehension:

children.text: tvaṃ cañcalo yad iha mādhava nāviko'si ||270||
children.translated_text: that you, O <s>Mādhava</s>, the fickle one, are the boatman here!" ||270||

body.translated_text: These two are by the compiler. (UN 15.236)

children.translated_text: "The boat is old, the river has exceedingly deep waters,
we are young girls — all this is a cause for calamity.
Yet the sole seed of deliverance for us slender-waisted women

children.text: yan mādhava tvam asi samprati karṇadhāraḥ ||271||
children.translated_text: is that you, O <s>Mādhava</s>, are now the helmsman!" ||271||
In the waters of the daughter of the sun,
that son of <s>Devakī</s> has stopped the boat.
He looks with a smile at the frightened face
of the <s>gopī</s> who has no means of crossing, bereft of a ferry. ||272||
"By your words alone, O joy of the <s>Yadu</s>s, the load of dairy goods,
and even my necklace, have been hastily scattered into the water by me.
And the silk garment from these two breasts has been cast away —
yet the bank of <s>Kalinda</s>'s daughter is still not near!" ||273||

children.text: payaḥ-pūraiḥ pūrṇā sapadi gataghūrṇā ca pavanair
children.translated_text: Filled to the brim with water, and now spinning from the winds,
this boat enters the deep waters of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā).
Alas, my misfortune! Yet <s>Hari</s>, his heart overwhelmed with supreme delight,

children.text: harir vāraṃ vāraṃ tad api karatāliṃ racayati ||274||
children.translated_text: claps his hands again and again! ||274||
"I have no hands free for the task of bailing out water,
and yet you make jokes as I rest!

children.text: jīvāmi cet punar ahaṃ na tadā kadāpi
children.translated_text: If I survive, then never again
will I set my feet upon your boat, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!" ||275||
"With this in mind, O friends,
bow to your desired deity!
Whether the <s>Yamunā</s> be only knee-deep
or not — let there be another boatman!" ||276||
"The boat is rickety, the river is deep,
and the fickle son of <s>Nanda</s> is the helmsman.
I am a helpless girl, the sun is setting,
the town is far, O friend — what shall I do here?" ||277||
"He does not heed words of praise, nor does he listen to plaintive entreaties,
he pays no regard to the prostrations that have been constantly offered.

children.text: hā kiṃ vidheyam adhunā sakhi nanda-sūnur
children.translated_text: Alas, what is to be done now, O friend? The son of <s>Nanda</s>,
in the middle of the river, the fickle one, shakes the boat!" ||278||

body.text: Extra verse found in only one edition.
body.translated_text: Extra verse found in only one edition.

children.translated_text: "For the sake of lightening the ferry's load,
O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, I take hold of your boat.
You make a bargain where there is none —
there is no trust in a boatman-fellow!"
"This daughter of the sun, whose banks are overleapt by towering waves,

children.text: pūrṇeyaṃ tarir ambubhir na hi hareḥ śaṅkā kalaṅkād api |
children.translated_text: this boat is full of water — and from <s>Hari</s> there is no assurance, not even from blemish.

children.text: kāṭhiṇyaṃ bhaja nādya sundari vayaṃ rādhe prasādena te
children.translated_text: Do not be hard-hearted today, O beautiful one — O <s>Rādhā</s>, by your grace, we —"
we live — clearly! Come, make the festival of sport in the mountain-valley! ||279||
You plead and whine, you who hide your limbs amid the heap of cow-dung in the corner of the house —

children.text: gūḍhāṅga kiṃ nanu vṛthā kitava prayāhi |
children.translated_text: why? In vain, O cheat, go away!
Where today is the cleverness of mocking
the host of cowherd women, terrified of the broken boat? ||280||

body.translated_text: The [above] three are by the compiler: (UN 5.49)
Now, the witty repartee of <s>Hari</s> with <s>Rādhā</s>:

body.text:
aṅgulyā kaḥ kavāṭaṃ praharati kuṭile mādhavaḥ kiṃ vasanto
no cakrī kiṃ kulālo na hi dharaṇī-dharaḥ kiṃ dvijihvaḥ phaṇīndraḥ |
nāhaṃ ghorāhi-mardī kim asi khaga-patir no hariḥ kiṃ kapīśo
rādhā-vāṇībhir itthaṃ prahasita-vadanaḥ pātu vaś cakra-pāṇiḥ ||281|| kasyacit || (Sbhv 130; KK 3.105; Srk 7.19)
body.translated_text: 'Who strikes the door with his finger?' 'O crooked one, <s>Mādhava</s>.' 'What, the spring?' 'No, the disc-bearer.' 'What, a potter?' 'No, the upholder of the earth.' 'What, the two-tongued one, the serpent-king?' 'I am not the slayer of terrible serpents.' 'Are you the lord of birds (<s>Garuḍa</s>)?' 'No, <s>Hari</s>.' 'What, the monkey-lord?' — Thus, with a smiling face at <s>Rādhā</s>'s words, may <s>Cakrapāṇi</s> (the disc-handed one) protect you! ||281||

children.text: kas tvaṃ bho niśi keśavaḥ śirasijai :y kiṃ nāma garvāyase
children.translated_text: 'Who are you, sir, at night?' '<s>Keśava</s>.' 'By your long hair? Why do you pride yourself?'

children.text: bhadre śaurir ahaṃ guṇaiḥ pitṛ-gataiḥ putrasya kiṃ syād iha |
children.translated_text: 'Dear lady, I am <s>Śauri</s>.' 'By the qualities inherited from your father? What would the son have here?'

children.text: cakrī candramukhi prayacchasi na me kuṇḍīṃ ghaṭīṃ dohanīm
children.translated_text: '[I am] the disc-bearer, O moon-face.' 'You will not give me a pot, a pitcher, or a milking-pail?'

children.text: itthaṃ gopa-vadhū-jitottaratayā hrīṇo hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||282||
children.translated_text: Thus, embarrassed by the victorious retorts of the cowherd woman, may <s>Hari</s> protect you! ||282||

children.text: vāsaḥ samprati keśava kva bhavato mugdhekṣaṇe nanv idaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Where is your garment now, O <s>Keśava</s>?' 'O innocent-eyed one, this very one.'
'Tell [me about] the garment, O rogue — O beauty, [it has changed] from contact with your body.'

children.text: yāminyām uṣitaḥ kva dhūrta vitanur muṣṇāti kiṃ yāminī
children.translated_text: 'Where did you stay the night?' 'O scoundrel, does the night make one thin? Does the night steal?'

children.text: śaurir gopavadhūṃ chalaiḥ parihasann evaṃvidhaiḥ pātu vaḥ ||283||
children.translated_text: <s>Śauri</s>, thus jesting with the cowherd woman by such deceits, may he protect you! ||283||

children.text: rādhe tvaṃ kupitā tvam eva kupitā ruṣṭāsi bhūmer yato
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>, you are angry, you yourself are angry, you are offended — because of the earth,

children.text: mātā tvaṃ jagatāṃ tvam eva jagatāṃ mātā na vijño'paraḥ |
children.translated_text: you are the mother of the worlds, you yourself are the mother of the worlds — no one else is wiser.'

children.text: devi tvaṃ parihāsa-keli-kalahe'nantā tvam evety asau
children.translated_text: 'O goddess, in this quarrel of playful sport, you are infinite, you yourself are [infinite]' — thus

children.text: smero vallava-sundarīm avanamac chauriḥ śriyaḥ vaḥ kriyāt ||284||
children.translated_text: smiling, <s>Śauri</s> bowed to the beautiful cowherd woman. May he bestow splendor upon you! ||284||
In the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s>, in the abode of joy, in the fragrance of jasmine flowers,
beautiful with the rays of the resplendent moon, charming with cuckoos and others —
at night, wondrous, stealing the minds and bodies of the cowherd women,
the splendor of the sweet flute-playing of the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> shone forth! ||285||
Pre-eminent in the sweetness of the nectar of the lips,
this sound of the flute of <s>Hari</s>'s play —
it spread the delight of the mind exceedingly
among the does and the doe-eyed [women] and the sages. ||286||
He whose flute made melodious by play
has assembled the host of cowherd women —
thirsting for the honey of his lips,
may <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> protect you from harm! ||287||
'Do not delay, O mother,
release my hand — I go to <s>Hari</s>!
I cannot bear to stay, for he
thunders on his flute like a bold female messenger!' ||288||
His hair kissed by the beautiful crescent moon on his crest, his garment golden,
a <s>karṇikāra</s> flower adorning his ear, surging with the sport of <s>Kandarpa</s>,
his face eloquent with the playing of the flute, his glance sidelong —
the fortune ripened — the slender-waisted ones entered the inner bower! ||289||

children.text: duṣṭaḥ ko'pi karoti vaḥ paribhavaṃ śaṅke muhur gokule
children.translated_text: 'Some wicked one is assaulting you — I suspect, repeatedly — in <s>Gokula</s>;

children.text: dhāvantyaḥ skhalad-ambaraṃ niśi vane yūyaṃ yad-abhyāgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: for you come running at night to the forest, with garments slipping!
Ah, what fear — when on my arm, which bears the vermilion mark from the foreheads of the wives of the demon <s>Manda</s>,

children.text: dordaṇḍe mama bhāti dīvyata pati-kroḍe kuraṅgī-dṛśaḥ ||290||
children.translated_text: [there is strength]? Sport, O doe-eyed ones, in the lap of your husbands!' ||290||
'In the dense flood of <s>dharma</s> flowing within <s>Vraja</s>, having dispelled the heat —

children.text: kā vas tṛṣṇā valati hṛdaye durmadeyaṃ satīnām |
children.translated_text: what craving stirs in your hearts? This is unseemly for virtuous wives!

children.text: sīmantinyaḥ spṛhayata gṛhān mā viruddhaṃ kurudhvaṃ
children.translated_text: O married women, desire [only] your homes; do not act against [propriety] —

children.text: nāyaṃ dṛṣṭau mama vighaṭate hanta puṇyasya panthāḥ || 291 ||
children.translated_text: alas, this path of merit is not obstructed in my sight!' ||291||
'How can you instruct us on the path of <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: prasīda svāṃ śiṣyām atikhilamukhīṃ śādhi muralīm |
children.translated_text: Be pleased — discipline your own disciple, the fully shameless flute!

children.text: harantī maryādāṃ śiva śiva pare puṃsi hṛdayaṃ
children.translated_text: Stealing our modesty, O <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>! Leading the heart to another man —

children.text: nayantī dhṛṣṭeyaṃ yaduvara yathā nāhvayati naḥ ||292 ||
children.translated_text: this bold one, O best of <s>Yadus</s>, summons us!' ||292||

body.translated_text: The [above] three are by the compiler:

children.translated_text: His middle embraced by the multitude of <s>gopīs</s>,
playing the flute, with exceedingly restless eyes,
goosebumps manifesting on his body —
I bow to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sole root of the universe! ||293||

children.text: kālindyāḥ pulineṣu keli-kupitām utsṛjya rāse rasaṃ
children.translated_text: Having abandoned <s>Rādhikā</s> in the <s>rāsa</s>-dance on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s>, angry from the sport of love,
as she went away weeping, and the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> followed her —
he who placed his feet in the footprints of her feet, with goosebumps rising,
may the unbroken entreaty of him who beheld his beloved appeased nourish you! ||294||

children.text: tulasi vilasasi tvaṃ malli jātāsi phullā
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Tulasī</s>, you delight! O <s>Mallī</s> (jasmine), you have bloomed!
O lotus of the land, O bee, you shine with your body attached [to flowers]!

children.text: kathayata bata sakhyaḥ kṣipram asmāsu kasmin
children.translated_text: Tell us, dear friends, quickly — in which
cave does the deceitful <s>Nanda</s>'s son, the root of guile, dwell?' ||295||

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ kvāpi sa mādhavo vraja-vadhūm ādāya kāñcid gataḥ
children.translated_text: 'That <s>Mādhava</s> has been seen somewhere — he has taken some <s>Vraja</s>-woman and gone!

children.text: sarvā eva hi vañcitāḥ sakhi vayaṃ so'nveṣaṇīyo yadi |
children.translated_text: We are all deceived, O friend — if he is to be searched for,

children.text: dve dve gacchatam ity udīrya sahasā rādhāṃ gṛhītvā kare
children.translated_text: go two by two!' — Having said this, suddenly seizing <s>Rādhā</s> by the hand,

children.text: gopī-veśa-dharo nikuñja-kuharaṃ prāpto hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||296||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, disguised as a <s>gopī</s>, entered a hollow in the bower. May he protect you! ||296||

children.text: adoṣād doṣād vā tyajati vipine tāṃ yadi bhavān
children.translated_text: 'Whether without fault or with fault, if you abandon her in the forest,

children.text: abhadraṃ bhadraṃ vā tribhuvana-pate tvāṃ vadatu kaḥ |
children.translated_text: whether it be wrong or right, O lord of the three worlds, who can say to you?

children.text: idaṃ tu krūraṃ me smarati hṛdayaṃ yat kila tayā
children.translated_text: But this is cruel to my heart — that she, indeed,
for your sake, in the wilderness, O ornament of your family, did not even consider herself.' ||297||
<s>Lakṣmī</s> being expanded in the middle of the <s>rāsa</s>-circle by his own self,
fragrant with musk, his moon-face placed upon the sportive flute,
with the circle of the playful <s>tāṇḍava</s>-dance seen all around by satisfied eyes,
may <s>Hari</s>, sporting, with feet resounding in the <s>hallīśaka</s> dance, protect you! ||298||

body.translated_text: Thereupon, the words of the celestial beings:

children.translated_text: 'That fruit sought by liberated sages —
some [indescribable] fruit — <s>Devakī</s> bears it;
<s>Yaśodā</s> nurtures it;
the <s>gopīs</s> enjoy it to their heart's content!' ||299||
'Austerities were performed by others;
the fruit thereof has ripened for the cowherd boys —
for the <s>Brahman</s>, upon the pitcher-like breasts of these [women],
reclines, blue like a sapphire!' ||300||
With a playful hand in the water-sport,
now releasing, now covering <s>Rādhikā</s>'s face —
may <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, delighting in the game
of separating and uniting the <s>cakravāka</s>-couple, protect the world! ||301||

body.translated_text: The envious words of <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s friend to <s>Rādhā</s>'s friend:

children.translated_text: 'Do not be proud that on your cheek there gleams
a fresh flower-pattern drawn by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s own hand —

children.text: anyāpi kiṃ na sakhi bhājanam īdṛśīnāṃ
children.translated_text: is no other woman, O friend, a fit vessel for such [favors],

children.text: vairī na ced bhavati vepathur antarāyaḥ ||302||
children.translated_text: unless the trembling of a rival becomes an obstacle?' ||302||

body.text: dāmodarasya | (Amaru 55; SKM 2.140.5 keśaṭasya; Smv 86.14; SD 3.105 mada; Daśa 2.22, etc.; BRS 2.4.165)

children.translated_text: 'Ever since in <s>Gokula</s> all around
rows of flower-strewn seats have appeared,
this one who loves yellow garments
has since become [fond of] <s>Candrāvalī</s>.' ||303||

body.translated_text: The words of a friend to <s>Candrāvalī</s>:

children.text: saujanyena vaśīkṛtā vayam atas tvāṃ kiñcid ācakṣmahe
children.translated_text: 'Out of goodwill we have been won over, and so we tell you something:

children.text: kālindīṃ yadi yāsi sundari punar mā gāḥ kadambāṭvaīm |
children.translated_text: if you go to the <s>Kālindī</s>, O beautiful one, do not go to the <s>kadamba</s> grove —
there is some utterly pure darkness there, in which,

children.text: lagne locanasīmni notpaladṛśaḥ paśyantī patyur gṛham ||304||
children.translated_text: when it barely touches the border of the lotus-eyed one's vision, she does not see her husband's house!' ||304||

children.text: śyāmo'yaṃ divasaḥ payoda-paṭalaiḥ sāyaṃ tathāpy utsukā
children.translated_text: 'The day is dark with masses of clouds; yet at evening, eager,

children.text: puṣpārthaṃ sakhi yāsi yāmuna-taṭaṃ yāhi vyathā kā mama |
children.translated_text: you go to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> for flowers — go! What distress is it of mine?

children.text: kintv ekaṃ khara-kaṇṭaka-kakṣatam urasy ālokya sadyo'nyathā
children.translated_text: But one thing — seeing the harsh scratch of thorns on your breast, suddenly

children.text: śaṅkāṃ yat kuṭilaḥ kariṣyati jano jātāsmi tenākulā || 305 ||
children.translated_text: the suspicion that the crooked-minded folk will form — that makes me anxious!' ||305||

children.text: gantavyā te manasi yamunā vartate cet tadānīṃ
children.translated_text: 'If going to the <s>Yamunā</s> is in your mind, then

children.text: kuñjaṃ mā gāḥ sahaja-sarale vāñjulaṃ mad-vacobhiḥ |
children.translated_text: do not go to the bower — O naturally innocent one, [go to] the cane-grove, by my words!

children.text: gacches tatrāpy ahaha yadi vā mā murārer udāre
children.translated_text: But ah, even if you go there — do not, O noble one, in the presence of <s>Murāri</s>,
anywhere alone in secret, listen to the sound of the flute!' ||306||
'O fickle one, do not delay —
remembering your water-pot, go home!
Before the enchanting <s>mantra</s>
is pronounced by the flute of the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>!' ||307||
Leaning his back against a <s>nīpa</s> tree, on the bank
of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), making the sportive flute resound, <s>Mukunda</s> —
even before the filling [is complete], as she swings her water-pot in the water,
he turns the face of the cowherd woman [toward him]! ||308||

children.text: sakhyo yayr gṛham ahaṃ kalasīṃ vahantī
children.translated_text: 'O friends, I am going home carrying a water-pot,
brimming full, exceedingly heavy — I am weighed down!
If you touch me while I am alone, O son of <s>Nanda</s>,

children.text: mokṣyāmi jīvanam idaṃ sahasā puras te ||309||
children.translated_text: I shall give up this life instantly before you!' ||309||

body.translated_text: The words of a certain [woman] to her:

children.text: valgantyā vana-mālayā tava hṛtaṃ vakṣojayoś candanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The sandal-paste on your breasts has been taken away by his swinging forest-garland;
the shark-shaped earring on your cheek has been shattered by the swinging of the crocodile [earring];

children.text: klāntā svaira-taraṅga-kelibhir iyaṃ tanvī ca dhūrte tanuḥ
children.translated_text: and your slender body is exhausted by the free play of waves — O rogue's [victim]!

children.text: satyaṃ jalpasi bhānujām abhi rase magnādya harṣād abhūḥ ||310||
children.translated_text: You speak the truth — you were today immersed in delight by the daughter of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>)!' ||310||

body.translated_text: The words of a friend to her husband:

children.translated_text: 'O handsome one, why do you look at my dear friend
repeatedly with suspicion?
Her back, yellowed by the scratches of her beloved's nails,
was [merely caused by] the wind from the <s>Yamunā</s>!' ||311||
'For what purpose, with desire for flowers of [the goddess] <s>Kātyāyanī</s>,
did you eagerly go to the hollow of the forest-interior?
See the thorn-marks on your pair of breasts —
the cowherd, O sweet-voiced one, alas, is looking angry!' ||312||
In <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, the eternal pastimes of <s>Mukunda</s> shine forth;

children.text: spaṣṭam eṣā rahasyatvāj jānadbhir api nocyate ||
children.translated_text: clearly, because of their secrecy, they are not spoken of even by those who know them.

children.text: tābhir nitya-vihāram eva tanute vṛndāvane mādhavo
children.translated_text: '<s>Mādhava</s> performs eternal sports in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>

children.text: goṣṭhāmbhojamukhībhir itya bhi manāk proce priyāyai haraḥ |
children.translated_text: with the lotus-faced women of the cowherd-settlement' — thus <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) briefly told his beloved.

children.text: līlāratna-rahasyatā vrajapater bhūyasy aho paśya yat
children.translated_text: 'The secrecy of the jewel-like pastimes of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> is great — see!

children.text: tattvajño'pi purāntare ca gamanaṃ vyācaṣṭa vaiyāsakiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even <s>Vyāsa</s>'s son (<s>Śuka</s>), the knower of truth, spoke of [his] going to the other city.'

children.text: tathā hi pādme pārvatyai vyājahāra haro rahaḥ |
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Padma</s> [Purāṇa]: <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) spoke secretly to <s>Pārvatī</s>:
'Where the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> sports in the company of cows, cowherds, and <s>gopīs</s> —'

body.translated_text: Now, the words of <s>Rādhā</s>'s friend upon <s>Hari</s>'s impending departure for <s>Mathurā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Today itself, the crescent moon that has just risen on the first day [of the fortnight] —

children.text: sakhyaṃ tvayā vapur idaṃ gamitaṃ varākyāḥ |
children.translated_text: its friendship with you has reduced this body of the poor one!
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has gone, O <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (Cupid), come that dawn,
tell me — upon whom will you discharge your volley of arrows?' ||313||

children.text: prasthānaṃ valayaiḥ kṛtaṃ priyasakhair ajasraṃ gataṃ
children.translated_text: 'Departure has been made by the bangles; the dear friends have gone ceaselessly;

children.text: dhṛtyā na kṣaṇam āsitaṃ vyavasitaṃ cittena gantuṃ puraḥ |
children.translated_text: fortitude did not stay even a moment; the mind resolved to go before [him];

children.text: gantuṃ niścita-cetasi priyatame sarve samaṃ prasthitā
children.translated_text: when the beloved has resolved to go, all have set out together —

children.text: gantavye sati jīvita-priya-suhṛt-sārthaḥ kim u tyajyate || 314 ||
children.translated_text: when there is a journey to be made, would one abandon the caravan of friends dear as life?' ||314||
She whose shadow never came within the path of his eyes,
that very woman now adorns the midst of the city.
Moreover, perceiving <s>Mukunda</s> in the city of <s>Mathurā</s>,
even a blind man, his hand placed in a kinsman's hand, sets forth. ||315||

body.translated_text: There, the words of the city women —

children.translated_text: "To shed tears unceasingly —
shame on us! Our eyes have become mere ears.
That which was worth seeing — that <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence) —
has already been beheld by the women of <s>Vraja</s>." ||316||

children.text: sāndrānandam anantam avyayam ajaṃ yad yogino'pi kṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: That which is of dense bliss, infinite, imperishable, unborn — which even <s>yogins</s>,

children.text: sākṣāt kartum upāsate pratidinaṃ dhyānaikatānāḥ param |
children.translated_text: intent upon meditation, daily worship to behold directly, even for a moment —

children.text: dhanyās tā vrajavāsināṃ yuvatayas tad brahma yāḥ kautukād
children.translated_text: blessed are those young women of <s>Vraja</s>'s residents, who that very <s>Brahman</s>, out of delight,
embrace, converse with, drag about in play, and kiss! ||317||
The root of bliss, the one essence of all the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas),
the light of the <s>Adhyātma</s> (supreme Self), exceedingly difficult to attain, dark as collyrium —
drawing him close, embracing him tightly between their full breasts at will —
the cowherd women have indeed attained him — ah, what heaps of merit they possess! ||
"Dear friend, that perverse-natured son of <s>Nanda</s>
has clearly not gone away with that city-man (<s>Akrūra</s>),
for the pond is like one with unbroken lotus leaves,
and the forest still has its foliage intact." ||318||

body.text:
yāsyāmīti samudyatasya vacanaṃ visrabdham ākarṇitaṃ
gacchan dūram apekṣito muhur asau vyāvṛtya paśyann api |
tac chūnye punar āgatāsmi bhavane prāṇās ta eva sthitāḥ
sakhyaḥ paśyata jīvita-praṇayinī dambhād ahaṃ rodimi ||319|| rudraṭasya |
body.translated_text: "'I shall go' — his words, spoken when he was about to depart, were heard with trust; as he went far, he was watched again and again, and he too kept turning back to look. Now I have returned to that empty house; my life-breaths remain as before. O friends, behold — I, who love life, weep only out of pretense!" ||319|| <s>Rudraṭa</s>'s |

children.translated_text: "One <s>yāma</s> (watch) has passed, two <s>yāmas</s> have passed,
all the <s>yāmas</s> have passed, the day has passed.
Alas, alas! What shall I do?
I do not see the face of <s>Hari</s>." ||320||
"On the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, tossing up
a ball of flowers in the guise of a dancer —
O friend, that moon-like youth disguised as a cowherd
will never be seen again!" ||321||
they are blessed, O friend!
But for us, now that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has gone,
even sleep, our enemy, has departed." ||322||

body.translated_text: "Those women who see their beloved in dreams,

children.translated_text: that is that very bower-tree — everything remains as before.
Alas, alas! But the one whose limbs are soft as a fresh rain-cloud —
that first incarnation of the flower-bowed god (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) — is not seen!" ||323||

body.translated_text: "This is that very spring season, that is that very grove,

children.translated_text: "A moment seems like an age,
my eyes are like the rainy season (streaming with tears),
the entire world has become void
in separation from <s>Govinda</s>." ||324||

children.text: dalati hṛdayaṃ gāḍhodvegaṃ dvidhā na tu bhidyate
children.translated_text: "The heart splits with intense agitation, yet does not break in two;

children.text: vahati vikalaḥ kāyo mūrcchāṃ na muñcati cetanām |
children.translated_text: the body, distressed, swoons, yet does not release consciousness;

children.text: jvalayati tanūm antardāhaḥ karoti na bhasmasāt
children.translated_text: an inner fire scorches the body, yet does not reduce it to ashes;

children.text: praharati vidhir marmacchedī na kṛntati jīvitam ||325||
children.translated_text: fate strikes at the vital points, yet does not sever life." ||325||
"Set the clouds adrift, pregnant with water; delight the <s>cātaka</s> birds;
make the peacocks eager with their cries; ripen the <s>ketaka</s> flowers;

children.text: virahiṇi jane mūrcchāṃ labdhvā vinodayati vyathā-
children.translated_text: having induced a swoon in the hearts of those separated from their beloved, O pitiless one, you revive them with consciousness —

children.text: makaruṇa punaḥ saṃjñā-vyādhiṃ vidhāya kim īhase || 326 ||
children.translated_text: what is this cruelty you perpetrate, inflicting the disease of awareness once again?" || 326 ||

body.translated_text: Both these are by <s>Bhavabhūti</s> | (Mālatīmādhava 9.42, Spd 3453; Smv 43.34)

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ ketaka-dhūli-dhūsaram idaṃ vyoma kramād vīkṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: "This sky, grey with <s>ketaka</s> pollen, has been seen; the horizons have gradually been surveyed,
bearing clusters of mushrooms; the breezes fragrant with <s>kadamba</s> have been endured.

children.text: sakhyaḥ saṃvṛṇutāśru muñcata bhayaṃ kasmān mudevākulā
children.translated_text: O friends, wipe away the tears, abandon fear — why are you so agitated?

children.text: etān apy adhunāsmi vajraghaṭitā nūnaṃ sahiṣye dhanān ||327||
children.translated_text: I am now surely made of adamant; I shall endure these thunderclaps too!" ||327||
"This is that very river; those are the very bees on the white water-lilies;

children.text: tad yāmunaṃ taṭam idaṃ vipinaṃ tad etat |
children.translated_text: that is the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>; this is that very grove.
Those are the very breezes fragrant with jasmine; you alone —
alas, O beloved of my life — have become unattainable!" ||328||
"O lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, when will my dwelling
proclaim that you have come,
with the moon-discs of their faces blooming,
running all around in every direction?" ||329||
"O Lord, whose heart melts with compassion for the wretched,
O master of <s>Mathurā</s>, when shall you be seen?
My heart, anxious without seeing you,
wanders — O beloved, what shall I do?" ||330||
"The separation from the moon of the cowherds does not so greatly
proclaim my anguish, O companion,
as does his dwelling in the city of the lord of demons (<s>Kaṃsa</s>),
surrounded by the cruel hordes of <s>asuras</s>." ||331||

body.text:
cūtāṅkure sphurati hanta nave nave'smin
jīvo'pi yāsyatitarāṃ tarala-svabhāvaḥ |
kiṃ tv ekam eva mama duḥkham abhūd analpaṃ

children.text: prāṇeśvareṇa sahito yad ayaṃ na yātaḥ ||332|||
children.translated_text: that it did not depart together with the lord of my life!" ||332||

body.translated_text: "Alas, when this fresh new mango shoot burgeons, even my life-breath, restless by nature, will depart all the more. But one thing alone was my great sorrow:

children.translated_text: "Clinging to the single thread of hope, I hang suspended

children.text: rakṣāmi jīvam avadhir niyato yadi syāt |
children.translated_text: and preserve my life — if only a fixed limit were set.
If not, then <s>Vidhi</s> (the Creator), the sole benefactor of all the worlds —

children.text: yat kāla-kūṭam asṛjat tad idaṃ kim artham ||333||
children.translated_text: for what purpose did he create <s>kālakūṭa</s> (the deadly poison)?" ||333||
"Spread forth, O <s>kunda</s> flower, your cool fragrance! O breeze, blow gently!

children.text: prakaṭaya śaśinn āśāḥ kāmaṃ manoja samullasa |
children.translated_text: O moon, reveal the horizons freely! O god of love, arise!
The appointed day has been fulfilled, O friends — cease speaking of him!

children.text: hṛdayam adhunā kiñcit kartuṃ mamānyad ihecchati ||334 ||
children.translated_text: My heart now wishes to do something else." ||334||

children.text: nāyāti ced yadupatiḥ sakhi naitu kāmaṃ
children.translated_text: "If the lord of the <s>Yadus</s> does not come, O friend, let him not come — so be it!
If my life-breaths depart from separation from him, let them depart!

children.text: ekaḥ paraṃ hṛdi mahān mama vajra-pāto
children.translated_text: Only one thing strikes my heart like a great thunderbolt:

children.text: bhūyo yad induvadanaṃ na vilokitaṃ tat || 335 ||
children.translated_text: that his moon-like face will never be seen again!" ||335||

children.text: pañcatvaṃ tanur etu bhūta-nivahāu svāṃśe viśantu sphuṭaṃ
children.translated_text: "Let this body perish; let the constituent elements clearly return to their own portions;

children.text: dhātāraṃ praṇipatya hanta śirasā tatrāpi yāce varam |
children.translated_text: bowing my head before the Creator, alas, even then I beg this boon:
let me become water in his ponds, light in his mirror, sky in the firmament
above his courtyard, earth on his path, and wind in his palm-leaf fan!" ||336||
"Let him embrace me, devoted to his feet, or let him crush me;
let him break my heart by not appearing;
let the libertine do with me as he pleases —
he alone is the lord of my life, and no other!" ||337||

body.text:
tāmbūlaṃ sva-mukhārdhaṃ carvitam itaḥ ko me mukhe nikṣiped
unmārga-prasṛtaṃ ca cāṭu-vacanaiḥ ko māṃ vaśe sthāpayet |
ehy ehīti vidūra-sārita-bhujaḥ svāṅke nidyāyādhunā
keli-srasta-śikhaṇḍakaṃ mama punar vyādhūya badhnātu kaḥ ||338|| tairabhuktasya ||
body.translated_text: "Who will place in my mouth half-chewed betel from her own mouth? Who will bring me, straying from the path, under control with coaxing words? Stretching out her arms calling 'Come, come!' and seating me on her lap — who will now retie my topknot that has come undone in play?" ||338|| <s>Tairabhukta</s>'s ||

children.text: yadi nibhṛtam araṇyaṃ prāntaraṃ vāpy apānthaṃ
children.translated_text: "If somehow, by the ripening of merit, I could obtain for a long time
a secluded forest or a pathless wilderness,
O moon-faced one, I would flood the worlds
with your sorrows, mingled with copious streaming tears and sobbing sounds." ||339||
"Among all objects of attachment, women are foremost;
among women, the <s>gopī</s>s, whose words are naturally gentle;
among them, she (<s>Rādhā</s>);
and in her, a certain sidelong glance — what can compare?" ||340||

children.text: āvirbhāva-dine na yena gaṇito hetus tanīyān api
children.translated_text: "On the day of its appearance, not even the slightest cause was reckoned;

children.text: kṣīyetāpi na cāparādha-vidhinā natyā nayo vardhate |
children.translated_text: by the course of transgressions it does not diminish, nor does it grow by propriety;
rivaling nectar, hostile to the sorrows of the three worlds —

children.text: premṇas tasya guroḥ kathaṃ nu karavai vāṅ-niṣṭhatā-lāghavam ||341||
children.translated_text: how can I reduce that mighty love to the triviality of mere words?" ||341||
"Let the capacity to compose words remain far away;
and let even the prospect of embracing your body remain far distant.

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ praṇatibhir idaṃ kiṃ tu yāce vidheyā
children.translated_text: But again and again, with folded hands, I beseech this one thing — may it be granted:

children.text: smāraṃ smāraṃ svajana-gaṇane kvāpi rekhā mamāpi ||342||
children.translated_text: that remembering me again and again, somewhere in the reckoning of your own people, there may be a mark for me too." ||342||

body.translated_text: The words of <s>Uddhava</s> as he goes to <s>Vṛndāvana</s> —

children.translated_text: "This is that <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), smooth and sweet as a blue-lotus petal,
beloved of the restless water-birds buzzing intoxicated,
on whose banks the foe of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) formerly spent his days
eagerly and thirstily in the pleasure of love-play with the <s>gopī</s>s." ||343||
"This very <s>Kālindī</s> formerly was made turbid day after day
with the colored waters tinged by the breast-paste of the young women of <s>Vraja</s>,
but now, alas, with the collyrium-darkened tears constantly shed by those weeping women,
now that <s>Murāri</s> has departed, it has become doubly dark!" ||344||
"This is that very bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> — here, hearing the fame of the slayer of the demon <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
<s>Gokula</s> became a place where food dropped from mouths mid-bite.
With the <s>gopī</s>s, whose voices were sweetly tender from hearing

children.text: svarābhir gopībhir diśi diśi samudghūrṇam aniśam ||345 ||
children.translated_text: the wandering sound of the flute, it resounded in every direction unceasingly." ||345||

body.text:
tābhyo namo vallava-vallabhābhyo
yāsāṃ guṇais tair abhicintyamānaiḥ |
vakṣaḥsthale niḥśvasitaiḥ kaduṣṇair
lakṣmīpater mlāyati vaijayantī || 346 || kasyacit ||
body.translated_text: "Obeisance to those beloved women of the cowherds, by whose virtues, when contemplated, the <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland on the chest of the lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) wilts from the warmth of his sighs!" ||346|| <s>kasyacit</s> (by someone) ||
The words of <s>Uddhava</s> to the community of goddesses of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.translated_text: "Even <s>yogins</s> are unable to traverse
the path that you, separated ones, have tread,
for you have attained the unattainable state of being the object of meditation
of the Supreme Person whose form is the object of meditation." ||347||

body.translated_text: The words of <s>Rādhā</s> to her friend upon seeing <s>Uddhava</s> —

children.text: kalyāṇaṃ kathayāmi kiṃ sahacari svaireṣu śaśvat purā
children.translated_text: "What auspicious news shall I tell, O companion? You who formerly, in intimate moments, always

children.text: yasyā nāma samīritaṃ muraripoḥ prāṇeśvaīti tvayā |
children.translated_text: uttered the name of the foe of <s>Mura</s>, calling him 'lord of my life' —

children.text: sāhaṃ premabhidābhayāt priyatamaṃ dṛṣṭvāpi dūtaṃ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: now I, out of fear of the very word 'love,' though seeing the dear messenger of the Lord,

children.text: sandiṣṭāsmi na veti saṃśayavatī pṛcchāmi no kiñcana ||348||
children.translated_text: am uncertain whether I have been remembered or not — I ask nothing." ||348||
"O fair-thighed one, do not stain
your moon-like face with the waters of eye-collyrium!
<s>Hari</s>, the ocean of compassion,
will bestow his grace upon you once more." ||349||
"With one cheek resting on the palm of her hand,
her face bathed in ceaseless streams of tears —
since the auspicious day of <s>Mādhava</s>'s departure,
how could even a trace of sleep come to the lotus-eyed one?" ||350||
"The merchants' houses are devoid of sandalwood,
the forests in distant regions are stripped of leaves,
even the rivers and lakes are bereft of lotuses —
yet the burning pain of separation from him has not abated!" ||351||

children.text: prāṇas tvaṃ jagatāṃ harer api purā saṅketa-veṇu-svanān
children.translated_text: "You are the life-breath of all beings; formerly, carrying the sounds of <s>Hari</s>'s signal-flute,

children.text: ādāya vraja-subhruvām iha bhavān mārgopadeśe guru |
children.translated_text: you were the guide showing the path to the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: haṃho mathurā-niṣkuṭānila sakhe sampraty api śrī-pater
children.translated_text: O friend, breeze of <s>Mathurā</s>'s gardens! Even now, your body purified and cooled by the touch of <s>Śrīpati</s>'s (<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s) limbs,
you alone are our savior!" ||352||
"With horripilation aroused by the gentle breeze coming from your land,
gratifying her eyes with a beautiful painted panel bearing your image,
her ears anointed with the nectar of your name, at the window facing the road to you —
of the slender girl, who stays day and night singing in the fifth note (<s>pañcama</s>), with words imbued [with longing]. ||353||
On the body, the fire of the fever of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One, i.e. Love); in the eyes, the seal of meditation;
on the throat, the breath of life; on the hand-shoots, the cheek reclining at length;

children.text: aṃse veṇī kuca-parisare candanaṃ vāci maunaṃ
children.translated_text: on the shoulder, the braid; on the region of the breasts, sandalwood-paste; on the lips, silence.

children.text: tasyāḥ sarvaṃ sthitam iti na ca tvāṃ vinā kvāpi cetaḥ ||354||
children.translated_text: Everything of hers is in [its] place — yet her mind is nowhere without you. ||354||
When the moon is seen, and the darkness has vanished, and it stands in the field of the sky,
blazing with spotless radiance — when you, her beloved, have gone far away,
her sigh becomes like a night-lotus bud, her face becomes like a lotus,

children.text: kṣīrodīyati manmatho dṛgapi ca drāk candrakāntīyati ||355||
children.translated_text: the god of love becomes like a milky ocean, and even her eye quickly becomes like moonstone. ||355||

body.text: bhīmabhaṭṭasya || (Spd 3480, Smv 44.10; SKM 2.36.1 first two lines somewhat different)

children.text: asyās tāpam ahaṃ mukunda kathayāmy eṇīdṛśas te kathaṃ
children.translated_text: The agony of this fawn-eyed one I shall describe to you, O <s>Mukunda</s> — how?

children.text: padminyāḥ sarasaṃ dalaṃ vinihitaṃ yasyāḥ satāpe hṛdi |
children.translated_text: A fresh petal of a lotus was placed on her burning heart.

children.text: ādau śuṣyati saṅkucaty anu tataś cūrṇatvam āpadyate
children.translated_text: First it dried up, then it curled, then it crumbled to powder,

children.text: paścān murmuratāṃ dadhad dahati ca śvāsāvadhūtaḥ śikhī ||356||
children.translated_text: and afterward, murmuring, the flame, fanned by her sighs, consumed it. ||356||
'The body-creeper might be blown away' — so she is not fanned with a lotus leaf.

children.text: sphoṭaḥ syād iti nāṅgakaṃ malayaja-kṣodāmbhasā sicyate |
children.translated_text: 'A blister might form' — so her body is not sprinkled with sandalwood-water.

children.text: syād asyātibharāt parābhava iti prāyo na vā pallavā-
children.translated_text: 'There might be, from its excessive weight, a collapse' — so scarcely are sprout-

children.text: ropo vakṣasi tat katha kṛśatanor adhiḥ samādhīyatām || 358 ||
children.translated_text: ornaments placed on her breast. How then is the treatment of her emaciated body to be administered? ||358||
which is as hard as diamond —
then truly, her welfare [is assured],
[for] it must be struck by the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (the god of Love) between you two. ||359||
'Fingernails are sprouting — cut them! The silk shawl slips — cover [her]!
[Bees] entering the pleasure-garden — frighten them off with the tinkling of bangles!'
Thus, among the sprout-trees, the gentle breeze, and the <s>kuhū</s>-voiced [cuckoos],
the coded exchanges of <s>Rādhā</s>'s friends with each other in your separation, O fortunate one. ||360||

body.text: śambhoḥ || (SKM 2.30.4 amaroḥ; Spd 3489 satkavicandrasya; Smv 44.13; SD 10.79)

children.text: galaty ekā mūrcchā bhavati punar anyā yad anayoḥ
children.translated_text: One swoon subsides and another arises — whether between these two there was

children.text: kim apy āsīn madhyaṃ subhaga nikhilāyām api niśi |
children.translated_text: any interval at all throughout the entire night, O fortunate one —
while she was writing a love-letter to the god of love on your behalf,
even the first section of the opening word '<s>Svasti</s>' (be well!) was not completed. ||361||

children.text: citrāya tvayi cintite tanubhuvā cakre tatajyaṃ dhanur-
children.translated_text: While she was painting you in a picture, the god of love strung his bow taut;

children.text: vartiṃ dhartum upāgate'ṅguli-yuge bāṇo guṇe yojitaḥ |
children.translated_text: as the pair of fingers came near to hold the brush, the arrow was fitted to the string.

children.text: prārabdhe tava citra-karmaṇi dhanur muktāstra-bhinnā bhṛśaṃ
children.translated_text: When the painting of your picture was begun, the bow released the arrow, and she, pierced,

children.text: bhittiṃ drag avalambya keśava ciraṃ sā tatra citrāyate ||362||
children.translated_text: quickly grasping the wall, O <s>Keśava</s>, became a painting herself for a long time. ||362||
Thinking you — matured through inner, steady contemplation — to be standing before her,

children.text: yāvad dorvalayaṃ karoti rabhasād agre samāliṅgitum |
children.translated_text: just as she eagerly makes a garland-loop with her arms to embrace [you],

children.text: tāvat taṃ nijam eva deham acirād aliṅgya romāñcitāṃ
children.translated_text: and immediately embracing her own body instead, [stands] horripilated,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vṛṣṭijalacchalena ruditaṃ manye payodair api ||363||
children.translated_text: seeing [her delusion], I believe even the clouds wept under the pretext of rain. ||363||

children.text: acchinnaṃ nayanāmbu bandhuṣu kṛtaṃ tāpaḥ sakhīṣv āhito
children.translated_text: Unceasing tears from the eyes; distress inflicted on relatives;

children.text: dainyaṃ nyastam aśeṣataḥ parijane cintā gurubhyo'rpitā |
children.translated_text: dejection deposited entirely among the attendants; anxiety entrusted to the elders.

children.text: adya śvaḥ kila nirvṛtiṃ vrajati sā śvāsaiḥ paraiḥ khidyate
children.translated_text: 'Today or tomorrow she will surely find peace' — [but] she is afflicted by deep sighs.

children.text: visrabdho bhava viprayoga-janitaṃ duḥkhaṃ vibhaktaṃ tayā ||364||
children.translated_text: Be assured: the sorrow born of separation has been distributed by her [among all]. ||364||

body.translated_text: Now, her words spoken in jealous love:

children.translated_text: 'Through the abundance of the sweetness of [your] face,
[you] who forcibly captivate the hearts of others —
for one who loves as a friend <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the <s>ātman</s>,
the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> — what hope is there for the body?' ||365||

body.translated_text: Now, the message of the <s>Vraja</s>-women, with sighing:

children.translated_text: 'What use are words, uneasy with the distress of a third person?
What use is a glance, weary with blinking?
O Lord, O son of <s>Nanda</s> — for the beautiful women of <s>Gokula</s>,
devotion to you alone is the inner companion, the friend, dwelling within.' ||366||
'[Those gopīs] who, by the sweet notes of the flute,
disregarded even the heavy burden of the elders' modesty —
in separation from you, how shall those <s>gopīs</s>
pass the time, O <s>Mādhava</s>?' ||367||
'O traveler on the road to <s>Mathurā</s>, of <s>Murāri</s>'s [city],
this is to be sung at the door — the words of the cowherd women:'
'Once again, in the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
the fire of <s>Kāliya</s>'s venom burns!' ||368||

body.translated_text: Now, the separation of <s>Hari</s>, who is in <s>Dvāravatī</s>:

children.translated_text: Remembering the <s>Kālindī</s> with its gently favorable current, dark as blue lotuses,
the mountain-slopes, the caves fragrant with <s>kadamba</s> flowers,
and <s>Rādhā</s>, sweet with the first tryst, born of longing —
may <s>Dāmodara</s>, the lord of <s>Dvāravatī</s>, bring delight to the three worlds! ||369||

children.text: kāmaṃ kāmayate na keli-nalinīṃ nāmodate kaumudī-
children.translated_text: He does not desire the play-lotus; he does not delight in the streaming moonlight;

children.text: nisyandair na samīhate mṛga-dṛśām ālāpa-līlām api |
children.translated_text: he does not seek even the sport of conversing with the fawn-eyed women.
Sinking at night, with exhausted body, with limbs sluggish from yearning for pleasure,

children.text: aṅgais tāmyati cetasi vrajavadhūm ādhāya mugdho hariḥ || 370 ||
children.translated_text: he languishes — the bewildered <s>Hari</s>, holding the wife of <s>Vraja</s> in his mind. ||370||
In the palace of <s>Dvārakā</s>, on the ocean tinted with the hues of jewels,
even while embraced by <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, with powerful horripilation,
may the faint of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> protect the universe —
that swoon of meditation upon the abundance of fragrance of <s>Rādhā</s>'s love-play in the <s>vānīra</s>-bower on the bank of the smooth <s>Yamunā</s>. ||371||

body.text: umāpatidharasya || (SKM 1.61.1; UN 14.184; Jīva and VCT to BRS 2.4.178)

children.translated_text: 'Submerged in the water by me through love, the bank was embraced [by her]' —

children.text: kenālīkam idaṃ tavādya kathitaṃ rādhe mudhā tāmyasi |
children.translated_text: 'By whom has this falsehood been told to you today, <s>Rādhā</s>? You are vainly distressed.'

children.text: ity utsavapna-paramparāsu śayane śrutvā giraṃ śārṅgiṇo
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech of the bow-wielder [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] on the bed, during a chain of talking in his sleep —

children.text: rukmiṇyā śithilīkṛtaḥ sakapataṃ kaṇṭha-grahaḥ pātu vaḥ ||372||
children.translated_text: may <s>Rukmiṇī</s>'s loosening of the neck-embrace, with a deceptive [excuse], protect you! ||372||
'Submerged in the water by me, out of fear of the god of love, her friend was embraced [by her]' —

children.text: kenālīkam idaṃ tavādya kathitaṃ rādhe mudhā tāmyasi |
children.translated_text: 'By whom has this falsehood been told to you today, <s>Rādhā</s>? You are vainly distressed.'

children.text: itthaṃ svapna-paramparāsu śayane śrutvā giraṃ śārṅgiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, hearing this speech of the bow-wielder on the bed, during a chain of dreams,

children.text: savyājaṃ śithilīkṛtaḥ kamalayā kaṇṭha-grahaḥ pātu vaḥ || kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: may the loosening of the neck-embrace by <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>/<s>Rukmiṇī</s>), with a pretext, protect you! || By an unknown author:

body.translated_text: Now, the separation-song of the Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>]:

children.translated_text: When the foe of <s>Mura</s> had gone to the city of <s>Dvāravatī</s>, [<s>Rādhā</s>],
covering herself with his garment, grasping the <s>vañjula</s>-creeper in the bower on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s>, with yearning,
sang aloud — with voice breaking in heavy tears and faltering syllables, in high-pitched tone —
a song by which even the aquatic creatures moving below the water cooed longingly. ||373||

body.text: aparājitasya || (SKM 1.58.4 kasyacit; Dhv, Vak 2.59; etc.; UN 14.188)

children.text: pāntha dvāravatīṃ prayāsi yadi he tad devakīnandano
children.translated_text: 'O traveler, if you are going to <s>Dvāravatī</s>, then tell the joy of <s>Devakī</s>:
the <s>gopīs</s>, enthralled by the spell of <s>Smara</s>'s enchanting <s>mantra</s>, have not forgotten [his] name.
These directions are robbed of light by curtains of dust from the <s>kadamba</s> trees of sport [now unused],
and the grounds on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> no longer enter your mind [as a place of remembrance].' ||374||

children.text: te govardhana-kandarāḥ sa yamunā-kacchaḥ sa ceṣṭāraso
children.translated_text: 'Those caves of <s>Govardhana</s>, that bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, that flavor of [your] pastimes,

children.text: bhāṇḍīraḥ sa vamaspatiḥ sahacarās te tac ca goṣṭhāṅganam |
children.translated_text: that <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> fig tree, those companions, and that courtyard of the cowherd settlement —

children.text: kiṃ dvāravatī-bhujaṅga hṛdayaṃ nāyāti doṣair apīty
children.translated_text: O serpent of <s>Dvāravatī</s>! Does the heart not come [to you], even through faults?' [they ask] —

children.text: avyād vo hṛdi duḥsahaṃ vraja-vadhū-sandeśa-śalyaṃ hareḥ ||375 ||
children.translated_text: may the unbearable thorn of the <s>Vraja</s>-women's message in <s>Hari</s>'s heart protect you! ||375||
'The sandbank of the <s>Kālindī</s>, the evening breezes, the lovely moonbeams —

children.text: santāpaṃ na harantu nāma nitarāṃ kurvanti kasmāt punaḥ |
children.translated_text: they do not remove our grief — rather, why do they intensify it?' —
Thus, [the message] entrusted by the <s>Vraja</s> women; as <s>Hari</s> listens in his inner chamber,
the sighs that issue forth, shattering the pride of his consorts' good fortune, are victorious! ||376||

body.translated_text: By the author of the <s>Pañcatantra</s>: (SKM 1.62.4; UN 15.164)
The words of the Lord of <s>Dvārakā</s> to <s>Mudāmāna</s> [<s>Uddhava</s>]:

children.text: mā gā ity apamaṅgalaṃ vraja sakhe snehena śūnyaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: '"Don't go" — that is inauspicious! "Go, O friend" — that is a word devoid of affection.',

children.text: tiṣṭheti prabhutā yathābhilapitaṃ kurv ity udāsīnatā |
children.translated_text: '"Stay" — that is a command, as if spoken offhandedly. "Do [as you please]" — that is indifference.'

children.text: brūmo hanta mudāma mitra vacanaṃ naivopacārād idaṃ
children.translated_text: 'We say, O friend <s>Mudāma</s>, this word is not merely a courtesy:',

children.text: smartavyā vayam ādareṇa bhavatā yāvad bhavad-darśanam ||377||
children.translated_text: 'Remember me with respect, so long as you have [not come for] my audience.' ||377||

body.translated_text: Upon seeing his [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s] own house and so forth, [<s>Uddhava</s>'s/a visitor's] words:

body.text:
tad-gehaṃ nata-bhitti mandiram idaṃ labdhāvakāśaṃ divaḥ
sā dhenur jaratī caranti kariṇām etā ghanābhā ghaṭāḥ |
sa kṣudro muṣala-dhvaniḥ kalam idaṃ saṅgītakaṃ yoṣitāṃ
citraṃ hanta kathaṃ dvijo'yam iyatīṃ bhūmiṃ samāropitaḥ ||378|| kasyacit ||
body.translated_text: That house has sunken walls; this temple has obtained an opening to the sky; that cow is old; these pots look like dense clouds and are [used by] elephants roaming about; that is the mean sound of a pestle — this is the melodious singing of the women! How strange — how has this twice-born one [Brāhmaṇa/Kṛṣṇa] been elevated to such a position! ||378|| By an unknown author:
Now, the pastimes of the Lord of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>:

children.translated_text: With the very [eye] by which the occasion of a new rising [of joy] was indicated,
[trembling] like a lotus struck by a fish;
closing the other eye, joyful <s>Rādhā</s>
beheld <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with that left eye alone. ||379||
The eye, veiled by the flood of tears welling up from bliss, is unable to see;

children.text: bāhū sīdata eva kampa-vidhurau śaktau na kaṇṭha-grahe |
children.translated_text: the arms sink, trembling and unsteady, unable to clasp the neck;
the voice has syllables and words broken by agitated stammering; the mind is restless with agitation.
Truly, even the union with the beloved, after a long time, becomes [like] separation! ||380||

body.text: śubhrasya || (SKM 2.132.1 kasyacit; Sbhv 2065 śrī-ḍāmarasya; Smv 54.10 kasyāpi)

body.translated_text: Now, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who is privately making amends:

children.text: kiṃ pādānte luṭhasi vimanāḥ svāmino hi svatantrāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Why do you roll at [my] feet, despondent? Lords are indeed independent!

children.text: kañcit kālaṃ kvacid abhiratas tatra kas te'parādhaḥ |
children.translated_text: For a while you found pleasure elsewhere — what fault of yours is that?

children.text: āgaskāriṇy aham iha yayā jīvitaṃ tad-viyoge
children.translated_text: I am the offender here — I who [continued] living in separation from you!
