children.text: bhartṛ-prāṇāḥ striya iti nanu tvaṃ mamaivānuneyaḥ ||381||
children.translated_text: "Women's lives belong to their husbands" — surely it is you who must be consoled by me!' ||381||

body.translated_text: By an unknown author: (SKM 2.47.1; Srk 643; Smv 57.14)

body.text: yaḥ kaumāra-haraḥ sa eva hi varas tā eva caitra-kṣapās

children.translated_text: those same <s>kadamba</s> breezes, mighty, fragrant with blossoming <s>mālatī</s> [jasmine];
and I am the same — yet, in the matter of the play of love-making,
the heart yearns for the bank of the <s>Revā</s>, under the <s>vetasī</s> (cane) tree. ||382||

body.translated_text: He who stole my maidenhood is indeed that very husband; those are the same <s>Caitra</s> nights;

children.translated_text: 'This is that very beloved <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O companion, met at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>;

children.text: tathāhaṃ sā rādhā tad idam ubhayoḥ saṅgama-sukham |
children.translated_text: and I am that very <s>Rādhā</s>; and this is the joy of the meeting of both of us.
Yet within, my mind, which delights in the sweet fifth-note melody of the flute,
yearns for the forest-grove on the sandbank of the <s>Kālindī</s>.' ||383||

body.translated_text: At the conclusion, the auspicious invocation:

children.text: mugdhe muñca viṣādam atra balabhit kampo gurus tyajyatāṃ
children.translated_text: 'O innocent one, abandon sorrow! Here stands <s>Balabhid</s> (<s>Indra</s>); let fear and its heaviness be cast away.

children.text: sad-bhāvaṃ bhaja puṇḍarīka-nayane mānyān imān mānaya |
children.translated_text: Cultivate sincere affection, O lotus-eyed one! Honor these who are worthy of honor!'
— While [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] was instructing <s>Lakṣmī</s> at the <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony), through the craft of <s>Dhanvantari</s>'s words,

children.text: ity anya-pratiṣedham ātmani vidhiṃ śṛṇvan hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||384||
children.translated_text: hearing in himself the prohibition of another [i.e. instruction to Lakṣmī to refuse others] as a commandment [for himself to approach] — may <s>Hari</s> protect you! ||384||

body.translated_text: Of someone: (<s>Sbhv</s> 84, of some Southern author; <s>SKM</s> 1.67.5, of <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>)

children.translated_text: To the crest-jewel of the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty,
to him who sports in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
to the savior who carries [us] across
the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> — homage to <s>Hari</s>! ||385||
The bracelets flashing from the collision with the whirling, radiant peak of Mount <s>Mandara</s>,
growing heavy from the weight of the trunk of <s>Puruhūta</s>'s (<s>Indra</s>'s) elephant,
cutting the leaf-ornaments shining on the cheeks of the wives of the lord of <s>Daityas</s> —
may the staff-like arms of the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, which steal away the sins of the terrible age of <s>Kali</s>, protect you! ||386||
The compositions (<s>sandarbhas</s>) that have been made here
by <s>Jayadeva</s>, <s>Bilvamaṅgala</s>, and others —
the verses of those [authors are not included here];
the rest have been collected here. ||387||
Radiant with the culmination of the brilliant <s>rasa</s> (<s>ujjvala-rasa</s>),
encircled by the protector-women (<s>pālikā</s>) of the <s>Gokula</s> clan —
may he grant what is desired:
a certain young <s>tamāla</s> wish-fulfilling tree! ||388||

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Padyāvalī</s>, compiled by the revered <s>Rūpa Gosvāmin</s>.

children.text: kṛtaṃ na sukṛtaṃ mayā kṛtam aho mahā-duṣkṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: I have not performed good deeds; alas, I have committed great sins.

children.text: kṛtānta-nagare gatir bhavatu me tatra kīdṛśī |
children.translated_text: What kind of fate awaits me in the city of the lord of death?

children.text: na bho na dinabhoga-dig-bhramaṇam asmāt paraṃ punas
children.translated_text: O [Lord], no more shall I wander astray in the pursuit of daily pleasures henceforth —

children.text: tathā kuru yathā taṭe tava ghaṭeta vāso mama ||
children.translated_text: act so that my dwelling may be established on your bank [i.e., at your feet].
from <s>Rādhā</s>'s lips, the glory of the primal <s>rasa</s>,
to the king of <s>Gopālapura</s>,
homage to you, O wearer of the yellow garment (<s>Pītāmbara</s>)!

body.translated_text: To him who bears the stream of nectar
